cd_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
cd_ground.text: Is the aircraft parked on the ground?
cd_ground.help: This start-up is for an aircraft parked at a gate. The answer is filled in from the simulator when it can tell.

cd_air.title: Not on the ground
cd_air.text: The start-up procedure is for the parked aircraft. Land and park first, or use the Descent, Landing and Shutdown topics. The FlyByWire guide assumes the aircraft is 'in a cold and dark state at a gate'.

cd_state.title: Is the aircraft powered?
cd_state.text: Are the cockpit displays on (aircraft powered)?
cd_state.help: Cold and dark means everything is off and the displays are black. The check uses AC bus 1: it is powered when external power, the APU or an engine generator supplies the aircraft.

cd_powered.title: Aircraft already powered
cd_powered.text: Batteries or ground power are already on. Continue with the steps that make sure the power source is the one you want, then the overhead panel set-up. The SOP says that if the aircraft was electrically supplied during the last 6 hours, the batteries go to AUTO and external power to ON.
cd_powered.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 4 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification; APU Fire Test) (Battery Verification)

cd_cockpit.title: Check the cockpit before power on

steps.text: Set the parking brake ON.
Check the speed brake lever is down and not armed.
Check the flaps lever is at 0 (retracted).
Check the weather radar is OFF.
Check both engine master switches are OFF.

check.code: (A:FUELSYSTEM VALVE SWITCH:1, Bool) (A:FUELSYSTEM VALVE SWITCH:2, Bool) +

steps.text: Check the engine mode selector is at NORM.
Check the thrust levers are at idle.
Check the landing gear lever is down.
Check the wiper selectors are OFF.
Set BAT 1 and BAT 2 to AUTO (no white OFF light).
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Batteries); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/ (BAT 1 + 2); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 3 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification)
steps.why: You hear chimes when the batteries come on. Batteries power only a small part of the aircraft. The SOP also checks the battery voltage is above 25.5 V after a long time without power; the ELEC page shows normal values from 25 to 31 V.

cd_power_q.title: External power
cd_power_q.text: Is external (ground) power available? A green AVAIL light shows on the EXT PWR button.
cd_power_q.help: Some gates and stands have no ground power, especially at small airports. That is realistic, not a bug.

steps.text: Press the EXT PWR button.
steps.why: A press with the green AVAIL light on closes the contactor and the white ON light comes on: external power now powers the aircraft.

steps.text: Wait about 50 seconds until the message FWS FWC 1+2 FAULT disappears from the ECAM.
steps.why: The Flight Warning System starts when AC power is available. Do not do the fire tests before it has finished. Alarms may sound when it ends.

cd_noext.title: No external power
cd_noext.text: Use the APU for power. If you want ground power anyway, the flyPad Ground page has a 'Connect External Power' button that calls a ground power unit when the airport has one.
cd_noext.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/ (Ground Service, Connect External Power); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Ground Power Not Available)

cd_apu_ask.title: APU
cd_apu_ask.text: Do you want to start the APU now?

choices.label: No, it is already running or not needed now

cd_apu_ask.help: The APU supplies power if there is no ground power, and bleed air for the engine start. The guide says to start it even with ground power (air conditioning, engine start).

steps.text: Press and hold the APU TEST button on the fire panel.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Overhead Panel, APU Fire Test); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 4 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification; APU Fire Test)
steps.why: The APU fire warning shows on the ECAM, the APU FIRE button lights red, the SQUIB and DISCH lights come on and a chime sounds. Do this test after the FWS start-up has finished (about 50 seconds after AC power). Without external power only the panel lights show and the ECAM stays dark.

steps.text: Press the APU MASTER SW button.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (APU); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 4 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification; APU Fire Test)
steps.why: The blue ON light comes on and the APU runs a power-up test. The SOP recommends waiting 3 seconds before pressing START.

steps.text: Press the APU START button.
steps.where: Overhead panel, APU section, below the MASTER SW button.
steps.why: The start takes about 1 minute.

steps.text: Wait until the green AVAIL light shows on the START button.
steps.why: AVAIL appears when the APU is above 99.5 % speed (or 2 seconds after 95 %). Then the APU can supply electrical power and bleed air.

steps.text: Press the APU BLEED button so it shows ON.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (APU, note on APU BLEED); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 4 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification; APU Fire Test) (Air Conditioning)
steps.why: Engine start needs APU bleed air. Real airlines wait about 1 minute after AVAIL before this (Beginner Guide, real-world note). Do not use the APU bleed if a ground air unit is connected (SOP).

cd_o2.title: Crew oxygen, ADIRS and lights
cd_o2.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Crew Oxygen Supply, ADIRS alignment, Exterior Lighting, Passenger Signs)

steps.text: Press the crew OXYGEN SUPPLY button so the white OFF light goes out.
Turn the three ADIRS selector knobs to NAV, in the order 1, 2, 3.
steps.why: This starts the inertial alignment. ON BAT lights for a few seconds as a self-test. The alignment progress shows on the ECAM. It can take several minutes; the MCDU flight plan work can be done meanwhile.

steps.text: Turn on the NAV & LOGO lights.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Exterior Lighting); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 17 (sections: White lights on the overhead panel; Recorder; EVAC; ADIRS; Exterior lights; Signs)
steps.why: It shows that the aircraft is powered. In this simulator NAV & LOGO has only the positions 2 and OFF.

steps.text: Set the STROBE switch to AUTO.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Exterior Lighting); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 17 (sections: White lights on the overhead panel; Recorder; EVAC; ADIRS; Exterior lights; Signs)

steps.text: Turn the SEAT BELTS sign ON.
steps.why: Real world: the seat belts sign is not turned on until fuelling is complete.

steps.text: Set the NO SMOKING sign to AUTO.
Set the EMER EXIT LT switch to ARM (middle position).
Check the LDG ELEV knob is at AUTO.
steps.where: Overhead panel, cabin pressure section, 'a bit higher up'.
steps.why: LDG ELEV means landing elevation. AUTO is the normal position.

steps.text: Set the cabin temperature knobs as needed.
steps.why: Simply turn the 3 knobs as needed.

steps.text: Look at the hydraulic panel: no white light should be visible.
Turn on all fuel pumps until no white OFF light shows.
steps.where: Overhead panel, fuel panel, just below the hydraulic panel.
steps.why: The guide says all 6: the four wing tank pump buttons and the two centre tank buttons. Fuel is needed for the APU and the engines.

check.code: (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:2, Bool) (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:3, Bool) + (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:5, Bool) + (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:6, Bool) +

steps.text: Hold the ENG 1 FIRE TEST button for at least 5 seconds.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (ENG Fire Test); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 18 (sections: Signs; Probe / Window Heat; Cabin Pressure; Air Conditioning; Electrical; Fuel)
steps.why: Check that the lights and aural warnings work. The ECAM shows the engine fire warnings during the test.

steps.text: Hold the ENG 2 FIRE TEST button for at least 5 seconds.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (ENG Fire Test); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 18 (sections: Signs; Probe / Window Heat; Cabin Pressure; Air Conditioning; Electrical; Fuel)

cd_main.title: Main panel and radios
cd_main.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Main Panel: Displays, Radio Panel, ECAM Fuel Page)

steps.text: Adjust the brightness of the PFD, ND, ECAM and ISIS displays so you can read them.
steps.where: PFD and ND knobs beside the PFD; ECAM knobs just in front of the throttles; ISIS + and - buttons left of the upper ECAM.

steps.text: Set the current QNH on the ISIS.
steps.where: ISIS, left of the upper ECAM.

steps.text: Set the RMP 1 active frequency to the ATIS and the standby frequency to the ground frequency.
Set the barometer reference to QNH on the EFIS panel (push the BARO knob if it shows STD).
steps.where: Glareshield, EFIS control panel. In MSFS pushing is clicking the knob up and pulling is clicking it down.
steps.why: Turning the grey ring behind the knob changes inHg / hPa. QNH makes the altimeter show height above sea level.

steps.text: Turn the flight director (FD) on: the button light is green.
steps.where: Glareshield, EFIS panel, just below the baro reference.

steps.text: Check on the upper ECAM that there is enough fuel on board for the flight.
steps.why: If not, load more with the flyPad Fuel page (see the flight plan topic).

cd_done.title: Start-up done
cd_done.text: The aircraft is powered, the APU runs and the cockpit is set. The Beginner Guide counts this as 5 of 7 items of the BEFORE START checklist. Next: set up the flight plan on the MCDU, then start the engines.

pa_q.title: Power and APU
pa_q.text: What do you want to do?

choices.label: Batteries only (no ground power, no APU)

pa_q.help: Priorities: engine generators come first, then external power, then the APU generator (ELEC panel briefing).

steps.text: Check the green AVAIL light on the EXT PWR button.
steps.why: No AVAIL light means no ground power at this stand. Call a ground power unit from the flyPad Ground page or use the APU.

steps.text: Press the EXT PWR button.
Make sure the APU is available, or an engine generator supplies power.
steps.why: If nothing else supplies power the aircraft goes dark. Engine generators have priority over external power; external power has priority over the APU generator.

steps.text: Press the EXT PWR button so the ON light goes out.
steps.why: External power must be disconnected before pushback.

pa_apu_on.title: Start the APU
pa_apu_on.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (APU Fire Test, APU); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 4 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification; APU Fire Test)

steps.text: Press and hold the APU TEST button on the fire panel.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Overhead Panel, APU Fire Test); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 4 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification; APU Fire Test)
steps.why: The APU fire warning shows on the ECAM, the APU FIRE button lights red, the SQUIB and DISCH lights come on and a chime sounds. Do this test after the FWS start-up has finished (about 50 seconds after AC power). Without external power only the panel lights show and the ECAM stays dark.

steps.text: Press the APU MASTER SW button.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (APU); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 4 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification; APU Fire Test)
steps.why: The blue ON light comes on and the APU runs a power-up test. The SOP recommends waiting 3 seconds before pressing START.

steps.text: Press the APU START button.
steps.where: Overhead panel, APU section, below the MASTER SW button.
steps.why: The start takes about 1 minute.

steps.text: Wait until the green AVAIL light shows on the START button.
steps.why: AVAIL appears when the APU is above 99.5 % speed (or 2 seconds after 95 %). Then the APU can supply electrical power and bleed air.

steps.text: Press the APU BLEED button so it shows ON.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (APU, note on APU BLEED); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 4 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification; APU Fire Test) (Air Conditioning)
steps.why: Engine start needs APU bleed air. Real airlines wait about 1 minute after AVAIL before this (Beginner Guide, real-world note). Do not use the APU bleed if a ground air unit is connected (SOP).

steps.text: Press the APU BLEED button so it is OFF.
Press the APU MASTER SW button so it is OFF.
steps.why: The APU keeps running for a 60 second cooling period if it supplied bleed air. After a bleed air use, AVAIL can stay on for a few minutes. Wait 2 minutes for the APU flap door to close before you cut the power, because that needs APU or external power.

pa_bat.title: Batteries only
pa_bat.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/ (BAT 1 + 2); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 3 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification)

steps.text: Set BAT 1 and BAT 2 to AUTO.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/elec/ (BAT 1 + 2); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 3 (sections: Engines; Weather Radar; Landing Gear; Wipers; Battery Verification)
steps.why: Batteries power only a small part of the aircraft. The SOP recommends starting the APU within 30 minutes of selecting the batteries to AUTO if you start it on batteries only.

pa_done.title: Done
pa_done.text: The power source is set. See 'Cold and dark start-up' for the rest of the cockpit set-up.

fp_pre.title: Before the MCDU
fp_pre.help: The Beginner Guide lists these prerequisites: aircraft powered (external power or APU), ADIRS set to NAV, a valid flight plan and the IFR clearance from ATC.

fp_nopower.title: Power the aircraft first
fp_nopower.text: The MCDU needs power. Use the topic 'Cold and dark start-up' (or 'External power, APU and batteries') first, then come back.

fp_method.title: How do you enter the route?
fp_method.text: Do you import the route from SimBrief, or type it in?
fp_method.help: SimBrief import needs your SimBrief / Navigraph account linked in the flyPad (Settings, 3rd Party Options, Link Account). Use the 'Detailed Navlog' option and the A20N airframe for SimBrief. Do not choose an arrival airport in the MSFS world map: it removes the INIT REQUEST button.

steps.text: On the MCDU press the MCDU MENU key, then select ATSU.
Select AOC MENU, then INIT/PRESS, then INIT DATA REQ.
steps.why: This prepares the MCDU to receive the flight plan.

steps.text: Open the INIT A page and press INIT REQUEST (LSK2R).
steps.why: This loads the route from SimBrief. If INIT REQUEST is missing, an arrival airport was selected in the MSFS world map; see Troubleshooting.
steps.warn: Departure runway, SID, STAR and approach are NOT imported. You add them in the next steps.

steps.text: Optional: on INIT A select WIND/TEMP (LSK4R), then WIND REQUEST (LSK3R) to load the winds from SimBrief.
steps.why: Press LSK5R to go to the next phase page (CRZ WIND). No need to request the winds again there.

steps.text: Press the INIT key on the MCDU.
Type the departure and arrival airport codes as DEP/ARR (for example EDDM/EDDF) and press LSK1R.
steps.why: If you have no stored company routes, the next screen shows company routes; select Return with LSK6L.

steps.text: Type your flight number and press LSK3L.
Type the cost index from your flight plan and press LSK5L.
steps.why: The sample flight plan of the guide uses 10. Take the value from your own flight plan (OFP).

steps.text: Type the cruise flight level (for example 240) and press LSK6L.
steps.why: This enters the flight level and the temperature at that level.

steps.text: On the F-PLN page press the LSK next to the departure airport, then select DEPARTURE (LSK1L).
Select the departure runway.
steps.why: Use the one ATC gave you in your clearance.

steps.text: Select the SID from the list.
Press INSERT* (LSK6R).
steps.why: The waypoints of the SID appear in the flight plan. Use the vertical slew keys to scroll. If the SID has an ILS, its frequency is filled in on the RAD NAV page when it is in the database.

fp_route_q.title: Route between SID and arrival
fp_route_q.text: Is the route between the end of the SID and the arrival airport already in the flight plan?

fp_enroute.title: En route airways
fp_enroute.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (Enroute Flight Plan, DCT Before a Waypoint)

steps.text: Press the LSK next to the last waypoint of the SID, then select AIRWAYS (LSK5R).
Type the airway and press LSK1L, then type the waypoint where you leave it and press LSK1R.
steps.why: Airways go on the left, waypoints on the right. Repeat for each airway of your route. You can string up to five airways on the AIRWAYS page.

steps.text: Press INSERT* (LSK6R).
For a leg with DCT (direct) instead of an airway: press the LSK of the starting waypoint, type the next waypoint and press LSK3R.
steps.why: LSK3R is the NEXT WPT field of the lateral revision page. If the new waypoint is already later in the flight plan, the waypoints in between are removed. Otherwise a discontinuity is created.

steps.text: Press the LSK next to the destination airport, then select ARRIVAL (LSK1R).
Select the approach (for example an ILS) with its runway.
steps.why: A letter such as Y or Z after the approach name tells apart approaches to the same runway that have different minimums or equipment.

steps.text: Select the STAR.
Select the approach VIA, then a transition if offered.
Press INSERT* (LSK6R).

fp_check.title: Check the flight plan
fp_check.text: Scroll through the F-PLN pages with the vertical slew keys, or select PLAN mode on the EFIS panel and look at the ND. A discontinuity between the STAR and the approach is normal: it separates two parts of the flight plan. Do not clear discontinuities after a MANUAL leg or between SID and route unless you fully understand the routing. Check the speed and altitude constraints against your charts.
fp_check.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (Planning the Arrival, Discontinuity, Viewing Flight Plan on ND); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/flight-planning/disco/

steps.text: Press the RAD NAV key and check the VOR and ILS frequencies.
steps.why: The aircraft tunes a VOR automatically near the airport, and the departure ILS if the SID has one. Check they make sense for your departure.

steps.text: If the departure ILS is empty, type its frequency (for example 109.50) or its identifier into the ILS field with LSK3L.
steps.why: Type the ident OR the frequency, not both: both gives a FORMAT ERROR. Without a valid localizer the RWY mode will not engage on take-off.

steps.text: Leave the arrival ILS to the aircraft, and check it again when you reach the arrival.
steps.why: With an ILS approach in the flight plan it tunes automatically once you are in climb phase and within 250 NM of the destination.

fp_load.title: Load fuel and passengers (flyPad)
fp_load.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/ (A32NX Configuration, Loading Fuel and Weight); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/ (Fuel Page, Payload Page)

steps.text: On the flyPad open Ground, then the Fuel page. Type the fuel quantity (or import it from SimBrief) and press the play button.
steps.why: Fuel is loaded only with the flyPad. The MSFS fuel window is blocked. After engine start only 'Instant' fuelling is possible.

steps.text: Open the Payload page, enter the passengers or the planned zero fuel weight (ZFW), and start boarding.
steps.why: Use only one of the two fields. ZFW and its centre of gravity are then calculated for the MCDU.

steps.text: Press INIT, then the horizontal slew key to reach the INIT B / INIT FUEL PRED page.
Press LSK1R once to load the calculated ZFW/ZFWCG into the scratchpad, and again to enter it.
steps.why: This works after boarding has started in the flyPad. The empty orange boxes fill. Without ZFW the aircraft shows INITIALIZE WEIGHT/CG on the MCDU after engine start.

steps.text: Type the block fuel in tonnes (for example 4.7 for 4631 kg) and press LSK2R.
steps.why: Take it from the ECAM fuel on board, the SimBrief flight plan, or press LSK3R twice to let the MCDU compute it. The MCDU computation is only a reference, and it is not yet accurate.

steps.text: Press the PERF key. In preflight it opens the TAKE OFF page.
Get V1, VR and V2 from the flyPad Performance page (take-off calculator) and type them into LSK1L, LSK2L, LSK3L.
steps.why: Without V2 the SRS mode will not be available on take-off. In the Stable version without the calculator, press LSK1L twice (then the same for VR and V2) to get a simplified calculation from the MCDU.

steps.text: Type the flaps setting (for example 1) and press LSK3R.
steps.why: 1 means CONF 1+F. In the FLAPS/THS field you can also enter the trim as /0.4DN or /1.5UP (nose down / nose up). Entering the trim is subject to airline SOP and is optional.

steps.text: If you use reduced thrust, type the FLEX temperature in degrees C and press LSK4R.
steps.why: Flex lets the engines run at less than TOGA thrust, using a temperature higher than the real one. Use the flyPad Performance page to calculate it; the guide's 60 is only an example. Without a FLEX temperature use TOGA.

steps.text: Type the transition altitude from your departure chart and press LSK4L.
steps.why: The guide's sample SID has 5000 ft. The thrust reduction and acceleration altitude default to 1500 ft above the runway, minimum 400 ft.

steps.text: On the pedestal ATC panel check the mode is STBY for now.
Double press the CLR key to clear the old code, then type the squawk code ATC gave you.
steps.why: As long as the four digits are not complete, the previous code remains.

fp_done.title: Flight plan ready
fp_done.text: The flight plan, fuel, weights and take-off performance are set. Next: engine start.

es_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
es_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?

es_air.title: Not on the ground
es_air.text: This topic covers the normal ground start with APU bleed air. Land and park first, then come back.
es_air.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Engine Start); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/engine/ (ENG MODE selector: IGN START in flight initiates continuous ignition)

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

es_push_q.title: Pushback
es_push_q.text: Do you need to be pushed back before you start?
es_push_q.help: The Beginner Guide pushes back first and starts the engines during or after the pushback, when clear of the terminal.

steps.text: Make sure all doors are armed and secure and the passengers are on board.
steps.why: You can check the doors on the ECAM DOOR page (SOP).

steps.text: Press the EXT PWR button so the ON light goes out.
steps.why: External power must be disconnected. The APU must be available.

steps.text: Check the APU BLEED button shows ON.
Turn the BEACON light ON.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Prerequisites); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 27 (sections: Before Start Checklist; Pushback/Start Up Clearance; Windows and Doors; Exterior Lights; Thrust Levers; ACCU Pressure)
steps.why: It tells the ground crew that the engines are about to start.

steps.text: Get push and start clearance from ATC.
Call the tug: flyPad, Ground, Pushback, Call Tug.
steps.why: The tug is attached at once. At some gates you see no tug, but the pushback still works.

steps.text: Release the parking brake.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/ (Pushback, Parking Brake); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 27 (sections: Before Start Checklist; Pushback/Start Up Clearance; Windows and Doors; Exterior Lights; Thrust Levers; ACCU Pressure) (Parking Brake and Nosewheel Steering)

steps.text: Push back with the flyPad buttons, or with the rudder and elevator axes.
steps.why: The map on the flyPad pushback page helps. Do not use two pushback systems at the same time.

steps.text: When the pushback is done: set the parking brake, then release the tug on the flyPad.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 28 (sections: ) (When the pushback is completed); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/ (Call/Release Tug)
steps.why: After the tug is released the NW STRG DISC memo stays for about 15 seconds. You cannot steer until it has gone.

es_before.title: Before the engine start
es_before.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Prerequisites, Engine Start); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 27 (sections: Before Start Checklist; Pushback/Start Up Clearance; Windows and Doors; Exterior Lights; Thrust Levers; ACCU Pressure)

steps.text: Check the APU is available and the APU BLEED is ON.
steps.why: The aircraft needs pressurized air to start the engines. A crossbleed start is not yet implemented in the A32NX, and ground air units are not available in MSFS.

steps.text: Check the BEACON light is ON.
Check the thrust levers are at idle.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 27 (sections: Before Start Checklist; Pushback/Start Up Clearance; Windows and Doors; Exterior Lights; Thrust Levers; ACCU Pressure) (Thrust Levers)
steps.why: A lever beyond the idle detent can cause a hazardous situation at start-up.

steps.text: Start the chronometer above the ND to time the engine start.
steps.why: First push starts the timer, the second stops it, the third removes it from the ND. It is optional, an aid to time the start (about 1 minute).

steps.text: Set the ENG mode selector to IGN/START.
steps.why: You hear the packs turn off. The lower ECAM shows the engine page. The SOP advises to wait until the amber crosses and messages on the upper ECAM have gone before the master switch.

steps.text: Set the ENG 1 master switch to ON.
steps.why: Watch the ECAM. The engine takes roughly 1 minute to complete its start sequence.

steps.text: Wait until engine 1 is stable at idle with AVAIL shown.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Engine Start, Start Engine 1); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 30 (sections: Automatic Engine Start) (ENG IDLE PARAMETERS)
steps.why: At ISA sea level: N1 about 19 %, N2 about 68 %, EGT about 520 degC, fuel flow about 290 kg/h.

steps.text: Set the ENG 2 master switch to ON.
steps.why: Leave the mode selector at IGN/START: you set it to NORM in the after-start items. About 1 minute to complete. The Beginner Guide (Jan 2025) starts engine 1 first; the older SOP PDF starts engine 2 first because it pressurizes the yellow hydraulic system. Airline procedures differ.

steps.text: Wait until engine 2 is stable at idle with AVAIL shown.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Engine Start, Start Engine 2); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 30 (sections: Automatic Engine Start)
steps.why: At ISA sea level: N1 about 19 %, N2 about 68 %, EGT about 520 degC, fuel flow about 290 kg/h.

es_after.title: After engine start
es_after.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (After Engine Start); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 32 (sections: Engine Mode; APU Bleed; Anti-Ice; APU; Ground Spoilers; Rudder Trim)

steps.text: Set the ENG mode selector to NORM.
steps.why: The SOP recommends waiting about 5 minutes before take-off to avoid thermal shock. Taxi time counts.

steps.text: Set the flaps to the take-off setting you entered on the PERF page.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (After Engine Start, FLAPS); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 32 (sections: Engine Mode; APU Bleed; Anti-Ice; APU; Ground Spoilers; Rudder Trim) (Flaps)
steps.why: If you taxi in icing conditions (rain, slush or snow), keep the flaps retracted until the runway holding point (contamination of the slat/flap mechanism).

steps.text: Arm the ground spoilers: pull the speed brake lever up.
steps.why: The lever must be at RET before it can be armed.

steps.text: Set the APU BLEED button to OFF.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (After Engine Start); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 32 (sections: Engine Mode; APU Bleed; Anti-Ice; APU; Ground Spoilers; Rudder Trim)
steps.why: All engine bleed valves open automatically.

steps.text: Set the APU MASTER SW to OFF.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (After Engine Start); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 32 (sections: Engine Mode; APU Bleed; Anti-Ice; APU; Ground Spoilers; Rudder Trim)
steps.why: Keep it on if you want the APU for something. Using it for a long time can cause a fuel imbalance (SOP).

steps.text: Set the engine and wing anti-ice buttons as required.
steps.why: Consider it when the temperature is less than 10 degC with visible moisture. See the 'Anti-ice' topic.

steps.text: Check the pitch trim.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (After Engine Start, Setting Pitch Trim Advice)
steps.where: Pedestal, trim wheel beside the thrust levers.
steps.why: A precise value is not critical: any trim in the green band is safe if the centre of gravity is within limits. The trim table is at the bottom of the FlyByWire checklist PDF. Autotrim becomes active at lift-off.

steps.text: Set the rudder trim to zero.
steps.why: The RESET button moves the trim to zero at 1.5 degrees per second.

steps.text: Run the AFTER START checklist.
steps.why: Items: ANTI ICE as required, ECAM STATUS checked, PITCH TRIM set, RUDDER TRIM neutral.

es_fctl_q.title: Flight controls check
es_fctl_q.text: Do the flight controls check now?
es_fctl_q.help: Airlines do it after the AFTER START checklist or during taxi. Either is fine.

steps.text: Press the F/CTL button on the ECAM control panel.
steps.why: The lower ECAM shows the flight controls page. Everything should be green.

steps.text: Move the sidestick fully in all four directions and watch the ECAM page.
steps.why: The ailerons and elevators should show the full range. Upward arrows show in the SPD BRK area when you move the ailerons.

steps.text: Move the rudder pedals fully left and right.
steps.why: The rudder symbol on the ECAM should move all the way to each side.

es_done.title: Engines started
es_done.text: Both engines are running and the after-start items are done. Next: taxi.

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

tx_noeng.title: Start the engines first
tx_noeng.text: Use the topic 'Pushback and engine start', then come back.

tx_air_q.title: On the ground?
tx_air_q.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?

tx_air.title: Not on the ground
tx_air.text: Taxi is a ground procedure. In the air, use the topics for climb, cruise, descent and landing.

tx_taxi_clr.title: Taxi clearance
tx_taxi_clr.text: Ask ATC for taxi clearance, write down the route and read it back. Use the airport chart to follow it. Check the warnings and notices on the taxi chart. Also check the ATC clearance for departure and confirm the MCDU data as you taxi, especially if the clearance changed.
tx_taxi_clr.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Taxi Clearance, During Taxi); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 34 (sections: Taxi Clearance; Exterior Lights; Parking Brakes; Thrust Lever; Brakes; Nosewheel Steering)

tx_lights.title: Lights and brakes
tx_lights.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Taxi, Moving the Aircraft); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 34 (sections: Taxi Clearance; Exterior Lights; Parking Brakes; Thrust Lever; Brakes; Nosewheel Steering)

steps.text: Set the RWY TURN OFF light to ON.
Set the NOSE light to TAXI.
Look left and right: ground crew away, no aircraft or vehicles close.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Moving the Aircraft, Before Moving Safety Check)

steps.text: Release the parking brake.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Moving the Aircraft); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 34 (sections: Taxi Clearance; Exterior Lights; Parking Brakes; Thrust Lever; Brakes; Nosewheel Steering)

steps.text: Check the brake pressure on the triple indicator is zero.
If the aircraft does not roll, add a little thrust: about 25 to 30 % N1.
steps.why: Do not blast the engines near the terminal. The aircraft can also taxi at idle. Steer with the tiller or the rudder pedals.

steps.text: Do a quick brake check: press the brake pedals briefly and check the pressure.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Moving the Aircraft); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 35 (sections: Taxi Clearance; Exterior Lights; Parking Brakes; Thrust Lever; Brakes; Nosewheel Steering) (Brakes)
steps.why: You do not need to stop; look at the brake pressure. Do not do it in a turn.

steps.text: If an arc shows above the brake temperature on the WHEEL page of the lower ECAM, turn the brake fans on.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Moving the Aircraft); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 35 (sections: Taxi Clearance; Exterior Lights; Parking Brakes; Thrust Lever; Brakes; Nosewheel Steering)

tx_speed.title: Taxi speed and tips
tx_speed.text: Straight line: up to 30 kt is reasonable (local rules may be lower). Around 15 kt in regular turns and about 10 kt in sharp 90 degree turns. Slow down while turning. The A32NX can taxi on idle thrust. Keep the taxi line between the PFD and the ND (the grey bar between the two is your reference) and slightly over-steer in turns. Never cross a runway without clear permission from ATC and a read back. When you cross, turn the STROBE lights ON and look both ways.
tx_speed.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Speed While Taxiing, Handy Tips While Taxiing, Crossing a Runway)

tx_checks.title: Take-off checks while taxiing
tx_checks.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (During Taxi: Takeoff Data/Conditions, AFS/Flight Instruments); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 36 (sections: Takeoff Data/Conditions; AFS/Flight instruments; ATC; Terrain Radar; Autobrakes; Final Verification)

steps.text: If the runway or take-off conditions changed: recompute the take-off data, revise the MCDU, set the flaps, and re-enter V1, VR, V2 and the FLEX temperature.
steps.why: Cross-check the revised data.

steps.text: Check the SID and transition in the flight plan against the ATC clearance.
Set the cleared altitude on the FCU.
If ATC wants a specific heading after take-off, preset the heading on the FCU.
steps.why: NAV mode is then not armed and RWY TRK keeps the aircraft on the runway track.

steps.text: Check both flight directors are ON.
Set the weather radar to SYS 1 if you want it, and the PWS switch to AUTO.
steps.why: In MSFS the radar shows only precipitation, and the PWS switch only clears the ECAM warning.

steps.text: Check the transponder code and mode for take-off.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (AFS/Flight Instruments, ATC code/mode); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 36 (sections: Takeoff Data/Conditions; AFS/Flight instruments; ATC; Terrain Radar; Autobrakes; Final Verification)

steps.text: Set the TERR ON ND as required.
steps.where: Main panel, TERR ON ND button.

steps.text: Set the autobrake to MAX for take-off.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (AFS/Flight Instruments, AUTO BRK MAX); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 36 (sections: Takeoff Data/Conditions; AFS/Flight instruments; ATC; Terrain Radar; Autobrakes; Final Verification)
steps.why: If you reject the take-off above 72 kt, the autobrake and spoilers act. The ECAM TO memo shows AUTO BRK MAX.

steps.text: Do the flight controls check if you have not done it yet (see Pushback and engine start).

tx_done.title: Ready for the runway
tx_done.text: The main take-off items are set. At the holding point continue with the topic 'Take-off'.

to_where.title: Where are you?

choices.label: Taxiing / at the runway holding point
Lined up on the runway, cleared for take-off

to_where.help: If you started the flight on the runway, skip the line-up part and choose 'Lined up'.

to_air.title: Already airborne
to_air.text: Use the topics 'Climb and cruise' or 'Descent and approach'.

to_hold.title: Before take-off checks (down to the line)
to_hold.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (1. Lineup, Preparation and 'Down to the line' Checklist); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 38 (sections: Brake Fans; Line-Up Clearance; Exterior Lights; TCAS; Approach Path; Sliding Table/EFB)

steps.text: Check the overhead panel: APU off and no lights visible (normal situation).
steps.why: Exception: the packs can be OFF if that is part of your procedure.

steps.text: Check the flight controls and the flight instruments.
Press the CALLS ALL button to tell the cabin crew.
steps.why: The cabin crew answers with 'Cabin Ready' on the ECAM.

steps.text: Check the flaps lever agrees with the PERF TAKE OFF page.
Check V1, VR, V2 and the FLEX temperature on the PERF TAKE OFF page.
Set the transponder mode to AUTO or ON.
Set ALT RPTG to ON.
Set the COM 1 standby frequency to the departure frequency.
steps.why: Tip from the guide: you can then change quickly after take-off.

steps.text: Press the T.O. CONFIG button below the ECAM and read the memo.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (Check ECAM); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 37 (sections: Final Verification; Before Takeoff Checklist)
steps.why: No blue writing should be visible: AUTO BRK MAX, SIGN ON, CABIN READY, SPLRS ARM, FLAPS TO, TO CONFIG NORMAL. The ECAM must show T.O CONFIG NORMAL.

steps.text: Set the weather radar to SYS 1 if you want it, and the PWS switch to AUTO.
If the brake fans are on, check the brake temperature: below 150 degC you can switch them off, above it delay the take-off.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 38 (sections: Brake Fans; Line-Up Clearance; Exterior Lights; TCAS; Approach Path; Sliding Table/EFB) (Brake Fans)

to_runway.title: Line up
to_runway.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (1. Lineup, Entering Runway); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 39 (sections: Brake Fans; Line-Up Clearance; Exterior Lights; TCAS; Approach Path; Sliding Table/EFB)

steps.text: Get the line-up clearance from ATC.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 38 (sections: Brake Fans; Line-Up Clearance; Exterior Lights; TCAS; Approach Path; Sliding Table/EFB) (Line-Up Clearance)

steps.text: Check the approach path is clear: look outside and use TCAS on the ND.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (Entering Runway); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 39 (sections: Brake Fans; Line-Up Clearance; Exterior Lights; TCAS; Approach Path; Sliding Table/EFB) (Approach Path)

steps.text: Set the TCAS mode to TA/RA (or TA only if parallel or converging runways make it better).
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 39 (sections: Brake Fans; Line-Up Clearance; Exterior Lights; TCAS; Approach Path; Sliding Table/EFB) (TCAS)

steps.text: Release the parking brake and roll slowly onto the runway.
steps.why: A rolling start is possible, but as a beginner stop on the centre line first.

steps.text: Stop on the centre line and set the parking brake.
steps.why: If you were only cleared to line up, wait here for take-off clearance.

to_below.title: Below the line: last checks
to_below.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (2. Takeoff, Preparation and 'Below the line' Checklist); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 40 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting)

steps.text: Set the PACKS as required.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (Preparation and 'Below the line' Checklist); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 39 (sections: Brake Fans; Line-Up Clearance; Exterior Lights; TCAS; Approach Path; Sliding Table/EFB)
steps.why: Some airlines take off with the packs OFF or APU bleed ON for more thrust. If you do, switch them back on at the thrust reduction altitude.

steps.text: Set the NOSE light to T.O.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (Lights at Takeoff); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 40 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting)
steps.why: RWY TURN OFF on, LAND lights on and NOSE at T.O. minimise the bird-strike hazard.

steps.text: Check the RWY TURN OFF light is ON.
Turn both LAND lights ON.
Check the STROBE switch is ON or AUTO.
steps.why: BEACON and NAV & LOGO are already on. WING stays off; it is only for the wing inspection and ice.

steps.text: Check the ENG MODE selector is at NORM.
Check the TCAS traffic selector is ALL or ABV.
Wait for the take-off clearance from ATC.
steps.why: 'Cleared for take-off' means you may start the take-off roll when aligned with the runway.

to_roll.title: Take-off roll
to_roll.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (2. Takeoff); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 40-42 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting; Below 80 knots; Reaching 100 knots; At V1)

steps.text: Release the parking brake but keep your feet on the toe brakes.
Push the thrust levers slowly to about 50 % N1 and wait until both engines are stable.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (A typical standard takeoff); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 40 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting) (Thrust Setting)

steps.text: Push the sidestick forward about half way (full forward if the crosswind is above 20 kt or there is a tailwind).
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (A typical standard takeoff); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 40 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting)
steps.why: It puts pressure on the nose wheel and counters the nose-up effect.

steps.text: Release the brakes and push the thrust levers to FLX/MCT (if you set a FLEX temperature) or to TOGA.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (A typical standard takeoff); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 40 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting)
steps.why: Use TOGA if the runway is short or no FLEX temperature is set.

steps.text: Check the FMA on the PFD: MAN FLX (with temperature) or MAN TOGA, SRS, RWY, A/THR armed.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (A typical standard takeoff, FMA); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 40 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting) (PFD/ND monitor)
steps.why: Armed: CLB (vertical) and NAV (lateral). The autopilot is off and the flight director bars show the guidance. If SRS does not show, see Troubleshooting.

steps.text: Keep the aircraft on the centre line with the rudder.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (A typical standard takeoff); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 40 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting) (Directional control)
steps.why: At 130 kt the nose wheel steering and rudder pedals disconnect automatically.

steps.text: At about 80 kt slowly release the forward pressure. At 100 kt the sidestick is neutral.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (A typical standard takeoff); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 40 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting)

steps.text: Keep your hand on the thrust levers until V1, then take it off.
steps.why: V1 is the speed after which you no longer reject the take-off. It is the cyan 1 beside the speed band. To reject, see 'Reject the take-off'.

steps.text: At VR pull the sidestick back smoothly: pitch up at about 3 degrees per second to a pitch of 15 to 18 degrees.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (A typical standard takeoff); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 41 (sections: Takeoff Clearance; Exterior Lights; Thrust Setting; Below 80 knots; Reaching 100 knots; At V1) (At VR)
steps.why: VR is the cyan circle on the speed band. Count 'one-one thousand, two-one thousand' to reach 15 degrees at five. After lift-off follow the flight director. Avoid lateral inputs, they can extend spoilers.

steps.text: When you have a positive climb, retract the landing gear.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (A typical standard takeoff); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 42 (sections: Below 80 knots; Reaching 100 knots; At V1; At VR; When Positive Climb; At Thrust Reduction Altitude) (When Positive Climb)
steps.why: Check on the gear annunciators and the WHEEL page of the lower ECAM that the gear is up. The autopilot can be engaged above 100 ft AGL.

to_done.title: Airborne
to_done.text: You are flying with the gear up. Next: the topic 'Climb and cruise'.

rto_info.title: Reject the take-off (RTO)
rto_info.text: Rejecting is the captain's decision. Below 100 kt consider rejecting for any ECAM warning or caution. Between 100 kt and V1 reject only for a fire warning or severe damage, sudden loss of engine thrust, a red ECAM warning, or one of these amber cautions: F/CTL SIDESTICK FAULT, ENG FAIL, ENG REVERSE FAULT, ENG REVERSE UNLOCKED, ENG THR LEVER FAULT. After V1 continue unless the aircraft will not fly safely. To reject: announce STOP, thrust levers IDLE, reverse thrust to the maximum available, check reversers and deceleration, cancel the audio warnings. When stopped: stow the reversers, thrust levers idle, tell ATC, parking brake ON, alert the cabin crew, do the ECAM actions. If you reject below 72 kt the spoilers and autobrake do not activate, so brake fully by hand. When in doubt about the autobrake, take over manually. With enough runway left you can select idle reverse at 70 kt.
rto_info.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/rejected-take-off/ (Rejected Takeoff Procedure, text of the procedure; Reasons for a Rejected Takeoff; warning about 72 kt)

cc_air.title: Where is the aircraft?
cc_air.text: Is the aircraft in the air?

cc_phase.title: Flight phase
cc_phase.help: The flight phase is read from the flight management computer: take-off, climb or cruise.

cc_initial.title: Initial climb
cc_initial.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (3. Initial Climb); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 42-44 (sections: Below 80 knots; Reaching 100 knots; At V1; At VR; When Positive Climb; At Thrust Reduction Altitude)

steps.text: When LVR CLB flashes on the FMA, pull the thrust levers back into the CL detent.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (3. Initial Climb); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 42 (sections: Below 80 knots; Reaching 100 knots; At V1; At VR; When Positive Climb; At Thrust Reduction Altitude) (At Thrust Reduction Altitude)
steps.why: The thrust reduction altitude is typically about 1500 ft above the runway (set on the PERF page). A/THR then shows in white on the FMA. After this you do not touch the thrust levers again until final approach, in normal flight. If LVR CLB flashes at once after lift-off, check the thrust reduction and acceleration altitudes on the PERF page.

steps.text: Press the AP1 button on the FCU.
steps.why: The FMA shows AP1 in white in the upper right. The aircraft climbs to the altitude selected on the FCU. The autopilot can be engaged above 100 ft AGL.

steps.text: If you took off with flaps 2 or 3: at F speed select flaps 1. At S speed select flaps 0.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (3. Initial Climb, Flaps during takeoff and climb); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 43 (sections: At Acceleration Altitude; Above Acceleration Altitude / Climb Phase)
steps.why: S and F are letters beside the speed band of the PFD. With CONF 1+F you select flaps 0 at S speed. For CONF 3, the Beginner Guide goes directly to 1+F at F speed.

steps.text: Disarm the ground spoilers (speed brake lever down).
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (3. Initial Climb); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 43 (sections: At Acceleration Altitude; Above Acceleration Altitude / Climb Phase)

steps.text: Set the NOSE light to OFF.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (3. Initial Climb); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 43 (sections: At Acceleration Altitude; Above Acceleration Altitude / Climb Phase)
steps.why: The lights go off by themselves when the gear is retracted, but you still move the switches to OFF in case the automatic turn-off failed.

steps.text: Set the RWY TURN OFF light to OFF.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (3. Initial Climb); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 43 (sections: At Acceleration Altitude; Above Acceleration Altitude / Climb Phase)

steps.text: If you switched the packs off for take-off, turn them on again.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (3. Initial Climb); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 42 (sections: Below 80 knots; Reaching 100 knots; At V1; At VR; When Positive Climb; At Thrust Reduction Altitude)
steps.why: The SOP recommends turning pack 2 on at least 10 seconds after pack 1, for passenger comfort.

steps.text: Above the transition altitude, set the baro reference to STD: pull the BARO knob.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (3. Initial Climb, After takeoff checklist); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 46 (sections: Climb; Climb Speed Modifications; Expedite Climb; Checklist; At 10 000 Feet)
steps.where: Glareshield, EFIS panel. Do the same on the ISIS.
steps.why: The transition altitude is on the PERF page. A flashing baro value on the PFD reminds you.

steps.text: Run the AFTER TAKEOFF / CLIMB checklist and call ATC Departure with your altitude.
steps.why: ATC will usually give you a higher altitude. If not, level off at the cleared altitude: the autopilot does that automatically at the selected altitude.

cc_climb.title: Climb
cc_climb.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (4. Climb); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 46-47 (sections: Climb; Climb Speed Modifications; Expedite Climb; Checklist; At 10 000 Feet)

steps.text: Set the newly cleared altitude on the FCU.
steps.why: Turn the knob. The outer ring changes the step from 100 to 1000 ft.

steps.text: Push the ALT knob for a managed climb (CLB), or pull it for an open climb (OP CLB).
steps.why: The aircraft manages thrust and pitch to reach the altitude at the selected or managed speed. The FMA then shows THR CLB, CLB (ALT armed) and NAV. In MSFS pushing a knob is clicking it up and pulling it is clicking it down.

steps.text: Passing 10 000 ft: retract the landing lights.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (4. Climb); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 46 (sections: Climb; Climb Speed Modifications; Expedite Climb; Checklist; At 10 000 Feet)
steps.why: The aircraft then accelerates to the climb speed from the PERF CLB page. Also switch the seat belts sign off when the flight is stable (no turn, weather).

steps.text: Repeat the altitude steps until you reach the cruise level.
steps.why: Climbs are usually done in steps, each cleared by ATC. Do not use V/S to climb as a beginner: V/S has priority over speed and the speed needs to be watched very closely.
steps.warn: Using V/S in the A320 is not recommended for beginners (Beginner Guide).

cc_cruise.title: Cruise
cc_cruise.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (5. Cruise); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 49 (sections: Cruise)

steps.text: Check that the aircraft is level at the cruise level, the autopilot is on and the speed is managed.
steps.why: The cruise speed comes from the PERF CRZ page.

steps.text: Review the ECAM memo and the system pages: ENG, BLEED, ELEC, HYD, FUEL, COND, F/CTL, DOOR.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 49 (sections: Cruise) (Cruise); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (5. Cruise)
steps.why: The cruise is the quiet time to double-check the systems.

steps.text: Every 30 minutes check the fuel on board, the MCDU fuel prediction and the flight plan figures.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 49 (sections: Cruise) (Flight Progress)
steps.why: Check the track and distance to the next waypoint at each waypoint. The fuel on board plus the fuel used should agree with the fuel at departure. The MCDU fuel prediction is not yet accurate in the A32NX.

steps.text: Follow ATC requests with the FCU: altitude, heading, speed, direct-to. See the topic 'FCU and autopilot'.
steps.why: At 200 to 300 NM from the destination begin the descent planning (topic 'Descent and approach').

cc_done.title: Cruise
cc_done.text: You are in cruise. For FCU changes see 'FCU and autopilot', for route changes 'Change the flight plan', and for the descent 'Descent and approach'.

fcu_basics.title: How the FCU works
fcu_basics.text: The FCU has two ways to guide the aircraft: managed (the flight management system flies the planned route and profile) and selected (you give the values). Managed is shown by three dashes and a dot next to the window; selected shows your number and no dot. The altitude window always shows your selected altitude. For the four knobs SPD/MACH, HDG/TRK, ALT and V/S-FPA: Push = managed, Pull = selected, Turn = change the value. In MSFS pushing a knob is clicking it up and pulling is clicking it down. If you turn a knob in managed mode without pulling it, you only preselect: the window goes back to dashes after 45 seconds (HDG/TRK and V/S) or 10 seconds (SPD/MACH). Always watch the FMA on top of the PFD to see what the aircraft really does.

fcu_q.title: FCU and autopilot
fcu_q.text: What do you want to do?

choices.label: Change heading / go back to the route
Autopilot and autothrust on or off

fcu_alt.title: Change altitude
fcu_alt.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/fcu/ (Altitude selector knob); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (4. Climb, 5. Cruise); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/descent/ (2. Starting the Descent)

steps.text: Turn the ALT knob to the new altitude.
steps.why: Range 100 to 49 000 ft. The outer knob changes the step between 100 and 1000 ft.

steps.text: Push the knob for managed (CLB or DES: the constraints in the flight plan are respected), or pull it for selected (OP CLB or OP DES: constraints are ignored).
steps.why: Managed descent (DES) follows a calculated profile, which can give very high or very low vertical speeds. The Beginner Guide advises users not familiar with it to use OP DES, which gives a linear descent. Do not start a descent without ATC clearance.

steps.text: Check the FMA (second column) shows the new vertical mode in green.

fcu_spd.title: Change speed
fcu_spd.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/fcu/ (SPD/MACH knob); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (5. Cruise); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 46 (sections: Climb; Climb Speed Modifications; Expedite Climb; Checklist; At 10 000 Feet)

steps.text: Pull the SPD knob to select the speed.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (5. Cruise, ATC requests specific speed); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 46 (sections: Climb; Climb Speed Modifications; Expedite Climb; Checklist; At 10 000 Feet)
steps.why: The current speed is preselected. Range 100 to 399 kt, and 0.10 to 0.99 for Mach.

steps.text: Turn the knob to the speed ATC asked for.
steps.why: The aircraft changes thrust at once to reach the new speed.

steps.text: To go back to the managed speed, push the SPD knob.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 46 (sections: Climb; Climb Speed Modifications; Expedite Climb; Checklist; At 10 000 Feet) (Climb Speed Modifications)

steps.text: To change between speed and Mach, press the SPD/MACH button.
Turn the HDG knob to the heading ATC gave you.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/takeoff-climb-cruise/ (5. Cruise, Course change with Selected Heading)

steps.text: Pull the HDG knob to fly that heading (selected heading mode).
steps.why: The aircraft turns to the new heading.

steps.text: To fly the planned route again, push the HDG knob (managed mode, NAV).
steps.why: Pushing it with a route that has a discontinuity ahead will not work; see 'Change the flight plan'.

steps.text: Turn the V/S knob to the vertical speed you want, then pull the knob.
steps.why: Range -6000 to +6000 ft/min. V/S guidance has priority over the speed: when the speed reaches its limit, the V/S decreases to protect it. Watch the speed closely.

steps.text: To level off at once, push the V/S knob.
steps.why: The FMA shows V/S = 0 in green.

fcu_exp.title: Expedite
fcu_exp.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/fcu/ (EXPED); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 46 (sections: Climb; Climb Speed Modifications; Expedite Climb; Checklist; At 10 000 Feet) (Expedite Climb)

steps.text: Press the EXPED button.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/fcu/ (EXPED); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 46 (sections: Climb; Climb Speed Modifications; Expedite Climb; Checklist; At 10 000 Feet)
steps.why: The aircraft climbs or descends with the maximum vertical gradient to the selected altitude. To go back to ECON climb, push the ALT knob.

steps.text: Press the DIR key on the MCDU.
Select the waypoint with the left LSK next to it. If it is not in the flight plan, type it and press LSK1L.
Check the yellow dashed line on the ND, then confirm with the amber DIRECT prompt (6R).
steps.why: The Direct guide names LSK 1L for the confirmation; the DIR briefing names the amber DIRECT prompt in 6R. Use the prompt your MCDU shows. A T-P waypoint (turning point) appears in the flight plan. Waypoints between you and the new one are removed. If you were in HDG mode, the aircraft goes back to NAV.

fcu_ap.title: Autopilot and autothrust
fcu_ap.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/fcu/ (AP1 AP2 pushbuttons, A/THR pushbutton); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 42 (sections: Below 80 knots; Reaching 100 knots; At V1; At VR; When Positive Climb; At Thrust Reduction Altitude)

steps.text: To engage the autopilot, press AP1 (or AP2) on the FCU.
steps.why: The button lights green. The autopilot can be engaged above 100 ft AGL. For an approach, the SOP engages both AP1 and AP2 when APPR is armed.

steps.text: To disengage the autopilot, press the red takeover button on the sidestick.
steps.why: Normally you do not disengage with the FCU buttons. A warning (Master Warning light, audio) accompanies a disconnection. A short press on the sidestick button gives only a short warning.

steps.text: The autothrust (A/THR) works with the thrust levers in the CL detent. Press the A/THR button to arm or disconnect it.
steps.why: The thrust levers never move by themselves; they set the maximum thrust the A/THR can use. Normally you disconnect with the red instinctive button on the thrust levers, or by setting both levers to idle.
steps.warn: Holding the red A/THR disconnect button for more than 15 seconds disconnects the A/THR for the rest of the flight (all A/THR functions incl. ALPHA FLOOR are lost until the next FMGC power-up on the ground).

fcu_done.title: Done
fcu_done.text: Check the FMA on the PFD to confirm the modes. See the other FCU functions in this topic when you need them.

da_air.title: Where is the aircraft?
da_air.text: Is the aircraft in the air?

da_ground.title: On the ground
da_ground.text: This topic is for the flight from cruise down to the approach. For the ground phases use the other topics.

choices.label: In cruise, planning the descent (about 200 NM out)
Descending on the arrival, setting up for the approach

da_plan.title: Plan the descent and the approach
da_plan.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/descent/ (1. Descent and Approach Planning); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 51-53 (sections: Descent Preparation)

steps.text: Read the STAR chart and note the altitude and speed constraints.
steps.why: Consider the STAR and approach route as optional: ATC may give you vectors. It is your task to plan the descent, not ATC's.

steps.text: Find the first constraint (a STAR waypoint, the final approach fix altitude or the runway elevation) and compute the distance you need to descend to it.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/descent/ (How to Calculate the Required Distance for Descent)
steps.why: Rule of thumb for a 3 degree path: distance in NM = altitude difference in ft x 3 / 1000, plus about 10 % margin. The guide's example: 32 000 to 14 000 ft = 54 NM, plus 10 % = 59 NM. More margin for tailwind, less for headwind. The flyPad has a Top of Descent calculator on the Performance page.

steps.text: Read the distance to that waypoint on the MCDU PROG page, and mark the top of descent (for example with a FIX INFO ring on the ND).
steps.why: A FIX INFO ring with the descent distance shows your top of descent on the ND. The ND also has a TOD arrow, but the calculation stays your responsibility.

steps.text: Get the destination weather and runway: ATIS (QNH, temperature, wind, transition level) and the approach chart.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/descent/ (Advanced Arrival Planning); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 51 (sections: Descent Preparation) (Weather and landing information)
steps.why: With the built-in MSFS ATC the ATIS is available only when you are close to the destination. The METAR can be requested on the MCDU ATSU/AOC page.

steps.text: On the MCDU open the PERF page, go to the APPR page and enter QNH, TEMP, MAG WIND and TRANS ALT.
steps.why: Do it about 50 NM before the descent, or when the MCDU shows ENTER DEST DATA. The destination data is mandatory within 180 NM. A wrong QNH gives a wrong cabin pressurization. If the chart has no transition level ('By ATC'), the guide suggests Trans Alt + 1000 ft.

steps.text: Enter the minimums: BARO for a CAT I ILS (DA/MDA). For CAT II/III enter RADIO; enter NO or NO DH when the chart has no decision height.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/descent/ (Advanced Arrival Planning, BARO and RADIO); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 62 (sections: Descent Preparation; Initial/Intermediate Approach; Glide Interception from Above; Final Approach; At 350 ft RA; At entered minimum + 100 ft)
steps.why: The SOP recommends NO in the DH field to avoid false auto-callouts for a CAT III approach.

steps.text: Check the landing elevation is shown as AUTO on the ECAM cruise page.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 53 (sections: ) (LDG ELEV)
steps.why: LDG ELEV AUTO shows in green on the CRUISE page with the associated value.

steps.text: Plan the autobrake: LO for long dry runways, MED for short, wet or contaminated runways.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 53 (sections: ) (AUTO BRK); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing)
steps.why: The SOP does not recommend MAX for landing.

da_clr.title: Descent clearance
da_clr.text: A few minutes before the top of descent ask ATC for the descent clearance. Do NOT start the descent without ATC clearance (unless you already have a descent instruction).

da_start.title: Start the descent
da_start.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/descent/ (2. Starting the Descent); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 54-55 (sections: Descent Initiation; Descent Monitoring; At 10 000 feet; Approach Checklist)

steps.text: Set the cleared altitude on the FCU.
steps.why: ATC gives step descents. If a STAR constraint is above your clearance, descend only to the constraint altitude.

steps.text: Push the ALT knob for managed descent (DES), or pull it for open descent (OP DES).
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/descent/ (2. Starting the Descent); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 54 (sections: Descent Initiation; Descent Monitoring; At 10 000 feet)
steps.why: DES follows the calculated profile and respects constraints. The Beginner Guide advises OP DES for users not familiar with managed descent. The SOP recommends DES at the top of descent in NAV mode. DES is not available in HDG or TRK mode.

steps.text: Monitor the descent on the PROG page (vertical deviation, required distance) and adjust.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 54 (sections: Descent Initiation; Descent Monitoring; At 10 000 feet) (Descent Monitoring)
steps.why: To descend faster, increase the descent speed with the selected speed: it gives better fuel economy than other methods. Managed descent in a hold is limited to -1000 ft/min.

steps.text: At the transition level, set QNH on the EFIS panel and on the ISIS.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 54 (sections: Descent Initiation; Descent Monitoring; At 10 000 feet) (Descent Adjustment); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/efis_control/ (Barometer Reference Selector)
steps.where: Glareshield, EFIS panel. Push the BARO knob, then turn it.

steps.text: Check there is no STATUS reminder on the upper ECAM.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 54 (sections: Descent Initiation; Descent Monitoring; At 10 000 feet) (ECAM STATUS)
steps.why: Note any degradation of the landing capability.

da_10k.title: At 10 000 ft
da_10k.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/descent/ (At 10 000 ft Procedure); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 55 (sections: Descent Initiation; Descent Monitoring; At 10 000 feet; Approach Checklist)

steps.text: Turn the LAND lights ON (extend them) and the SEAT BELTS sign ON.
steps.why: Landing lights cause drag because they extend below the wings. Follow the airline policy. The cabin crew prepares the cabin when the signs come on.

steps.text: Press CSTR on the EFIS panel on both sides.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/descent/ (At 10 000 ft Procedure); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 55 (sections: Descent Initiation; Descent Monitoring; At 10 000 feet; Approach Checklist)

steps.text: If you plan an ILS, GLS or LOC approach, press the LS button.
steps.why: The PFD shows the LOC and glide scales and the identification when a valid signal exists. Check the identification is displayed.

steps.text: Check the radio navigation aids on the RAD NAV page are tuned and identified.
steps.why: The A32NX can autotune. For NDB approaches select the reference NAVAID by hand.

steps.text: Run the APPROACH checklist.
steps.why: Items: BARO REF set (both), SEAT BELTS on, MINIMUM set, AUTO BRAKE set, ENG MODE SEL as required.

da_type.title: Approach type

choices.label: RNAV or other non-precision approach with FINAL APP
Non-precision approach flown with FPA (TRK FPA)

da_type.help: The SOP lists which guidance mode fits which approach: ILS: LOC G/S. RNAV (GNSS) with LNAV/VNAV or LNAV minima, VOR, NDB: FINAL APP. Localizer-only, ILS G/S out, LOC back course, VOR, NDB: FPA guidance.

ap_vis.title: Visual approach
ap_vis.text: The FlyByWire pages used for this guide give no separate visual-approach procedure. The landing preparation steps (gear, flaps, autobrake, spoilers, lights, checklist) and the manual landing steps apply to any approach. Fly the final approach stable at 1000 ft above the ground.
ap_vis.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing, 4. Landing)

ap_ils.title: ILS approach
ap_ils.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (1. Intercepting the ILS Localizer, 2. Intercepting the ILS Glideslope); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 61-62 (sections: Descent Preparation; Initial/Intermediate Approach; Glide Interception from Above; Final Approach; At 350 ft RA; At entered minimum + 100 ft)

steps.text: Check the ILS frequency on the MCDU RAD NAV page against the approach chart.
steps.why: The aircraft normally tunes it. The identification must show on the ECAM RNAV page and the PFD.

steps.text: Press the LS button on the EFIS panel if the LS scales are not shown.
Be at the altitude from the chart with an approach angle not larger than 30 degrees to the localizer.
Activate the APPR phase on the MCDU PERF page: press ACTIVATE APPR PHASE (LSK6L) and confirm.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (1. Intercepting the ILS Localizer); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/perf/ (ACTIVATE APPR PHASE)
steps.why: It is normally done automatically, but do it now at the latest. In APPR phase the managed speed follows the flap setting: S-speed after flaps 1, F-speed after flaps 2, VAPP after the landing flaps.

steps.text: Push the SPD knob (managed speed). The aircraft decelerates to green dot speed.
Select flaps 1 at about VFE minus 15 kt, but never before the speed is below VFE.
steps.why: The aircraft decelerates further for the next configuration. Be in CONF 1 at S-speed before you need flaps 2.

steps.text: When cleared for the approach and on the intercept course, press APPR on the FCU.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (1. Intercepting the ILS Localizer); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 61 (sections: Descent Preparation; Initial/Intermediate Approach; Glide Interception from Above; Final Approach; At 350 ft RA)
steps.why: The FMA shows LOC in blue (armed) and G/S in blue. The SOP then recommends engaging both autopilots (AP1 and AP2). APPR also arms the glide slope: the aircraft descends as soon as it captures it.
steps.warn: Do not descend without ATC clearance and only when you are on the localizer. To be safe use LOC first and APPR when cleared for the approach.

steps.text: When LOC shows green, report 'established' to the tower.
steps.why: The tower then gives the approach clearance, which clears you to descend on the glide slope.

steps.text: Select flaps 2 before the glide slope descent starts (check the speed is below VFE for flaps 2).
steps.why: Beginners should take flaps 2 before the descent. It is hard to slow down on the glide slope. The Airbus guidance is flaps 2 at about 2000 ft during the glide slope descent, if the speed is low enough.

steps.text: When the glide slope deviation marker is centred the FMA shows G/S in green and the aircraft descends. The radio altimeter comes alive at 2500 ft.
steps.why: If ATC wants a given speed (for example 160 kt until 5 NM), pull the SPD knob and set it, then push it again at that distance (see 'FCU and autopilot').

ap_final.title: Non-precision approach with FINAL APP
ap_final.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 65-67 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At the Final Descent Point; At Entered Minimum +100 feet; At Entered Minimum) (Approach Using Final APP Guidance); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/glareshield/fcu/ (APPR)

steps.text: On the F-PLN page check the approach. If TOO STEEP PATH shows after the final descent point, do not use FINAL APP.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 65 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At the Final Descent Point) (Descent Preparation)
steps.why: Also check the outside air temperature is not below the minimum on the chart, and do not use the vertical managed guidance if corrections are needed.

steps.text: On the PROG page enter the runway threshold in the BRG/DIST field.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 65 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At the Final Descent Point) (Descent Preparation)
steps.why: This lets you monitor the position during the approach.

steps.text: At 10 000 ft verify the navigation accuracy, and for RNAV (GNSS) that GPS PRIMARY is available.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 65 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At the Final Descent Point) (Descent)
steps.why: If the accuracy is low, use TRK FPA for the approach.

steps.text: Set the baro reference (QNH).
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 65 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At the Final Descent Point) (Descent)

steps.text: When cleared for the approach and the TO waypoint is the final descent point, press APPR.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 65 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At the Final Descent Point) (Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach)
steps.warn: The FCU briefing page says APP NAV and FINAL modes were not available in the A32NX (note of August 2021). Check the FMA; if they do not arm, use the FPA approach.

steps.text: Check APP NAV is armed or engaged and FINAL is armed (V/DEV scale on the PFD, blue arrow on the ND).
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 65 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At the Final Descent Point) (Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach)

steps.text: At the final descent point check FINAL APP is engaged, and set the go-around altitude on the FCU.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 65 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At the Final Descent Point) (At the Final Descent Point)

steps.text: At the minimum: if you have the visual references, continue; if not, go around. Turn the autopilot off at the latest at the MAP or the minimum use height of the AP.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 66 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At the Final Descent Point; At Entered Minimum +100 feet; At Entered Minimum) (At Entered Minimum)

ap_fpa.title: Non-precision approach with FPA
ap_fpa.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 68-70 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet ; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At 0.3 NM from the Final Descent Point; At Entered Minimum + 100 Feet; At Entered Minimum) (Approach Using FPA Guidance)

steps.text: On the F-PLN page check the approach. Ignore the V/DEV on the PFD if TOO STEEP PATH shows after the final descent point.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 68 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet ; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach) (Descent Preparation)
steps.why: For NAV FPA approaches 1 degree of difference between the MCDU and the charted final track is acceptable; for conventional radio approaches 3 degrees. In all other cases use TRK FPA.

steps.text: On the PROG page enter the runway threshold in the BRG/DIST field.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 68 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet ; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach) (Descent Preparation)

steps.text: At 10 000 ft verify the navigation accuracy (and GPS PRIMARY for RNAV).
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 68 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet ; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach) (Descent)

steps.text: Arm the lateral mode for the approach: NAV, or press LOC for localizer-only and ILS G/S out approaches when cleared.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 68 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet ; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach) (Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach)
steps.why: For back course localizer approaches use TRK FPA.

steps.text: Press the HDG V/S - TRK FPA button and set the FPA for the final approach.
