steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 68 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet ; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach) (Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach)
steps.why: The FPA value comes from the approach chart.

steps.text: At 0.3 NM from the final descent point pull the FPA selector and check FPA is engaged.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 69 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet ; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At 0.3 NM from the Final Descent Point; At Entered Minimum + 100 Feet; At Entered Minimum) (At 0.3 NM from the Final Descent Point)

steps.text: Set the go-around altitude on the FCU.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 69 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet ; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At 0.3 NM from the Final Descent Point; At Entered Minimum + 100 Feet; At Entered Minimum)

steps.text: At the minimum: if you have the visual references, continue and turn off the AP and the FD, then set the runway track. If not, go around.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 69 (sections: Descent Preparation; At 10 000 feet ; Initial/Intermediate/Final Approach; At 0.3 NM from the Final Descent Point; At Entered Minimum + 100 Feet; At Entered Minimum) (At Entered Minimum)
steps.why: If the AP is still on at the minimum minus 50 ft, the FMA shows DISCONNECT AP FOR LDG.

ld_air.title: Where is the aircraft?
ld_air.text: Is the aircraft in the air?

ld_ground.title: Already on the ground
ld_ground.text: Continue with the topic 'After landing and shutdown'.

ld_config.title: Configure for landing
ld_config.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 59-60 (sections: At Green Dot Speed; At 2 000 Feet AGL Minimum; When Flaps Are At 2; Exterior Lights; When Landing Gear is Down)

steps.text: Set the go-around altitude on the FCU (see the missed approach on the chart).
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 61 (sections: Descent Preparation; Initial/Intermediate Approach; Glide Interception from Above; Final Approach; At 350 ft RA) (Initial/Intermediate Approach); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing)
steps.why: The Beginner Guide skips this step. It is set when the ILS or approach mode is armed.

steps.text: Lower the landing gear, between 2500 ft and 1500 ft, typically 5 to 6 NM from the runway.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing, Gear down); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 59 (sections: At Green Dot Speed; At 2 000 Feet AGL Minimum; When Flaps Are At 2; Exterior Lights; When Landing Gear is Down) (When Flaps Are At 2)
steps.why: The SOP lowers the gear when flaps 2 are set. Check three green lights on the gear panel and the WHEEL page.

steps.text: Turn the RWY TURN OFF light ON and set the NOSE light to T.O.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 59 (sections: At Green Dot Speed; At 2 000 Feet AGL Minimum; When Flaps Are At 2; Exterior Lights; When Landing Gear is Down) (Exterior Lights)

steps.text: Select flaps 3, then flaps FULL. Check the speed before each selection.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 60 (sections: Exterior Lights; When Landing Gear is Down)
steps.why: Flaps FULL reduces your speed to VAPP. Too much speed gives an overspeed. Retract the speed brakes before selecting FULL (otherwise the aircraft pitches down when they retract automatically).

steps.text: Arm the autobrake: LO for a dry runway, MED for rain, snow or a short runway.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 53 (sections: )
steps.why: Maximum manual braking needs MED selected, reverse thrust MAX at touchdown, and full pedal braking on nosewheel touchdown.

steps.text: Arm the ground spoilers: pull the speed brake lever up (it must be retracted first).
Press the CALLS ALL button to tell the cabin crew.
steps.why: This sets the Cabin Ready status on the ECAM and plays 'Cabin Crew take your seats for landing'.

steps.text: Run the LANDING checklist: the ECAM LDG memo must show no blue item (LDG GEAR DN, SIGNS ON, CABIN READY, SPLRS ARM, FLAPS SET).
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (3. Preparation and Checklist for Landing); FBW A32NX Checklist.pdf
steps.why: Be fully set up and stable at 1000 ft above the ground. Keep your hand on the thrust levers for a possible go-around.

ld_mode.title: Landing method
ld_mode.help: Autoland needs a CAT II/III capable runway and the conditions in the Autoland page (see the next steps). The Beginner Guide teaches the manual landing.

ld_manual.title: Manual landing
ld_manual.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (4. Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 71 (sections: Flare; At Touchdown; At 70 knots; At Taxi Speed) (Manual Landing)

steps.text: Check you have the landing clearance from ATC.
steps.why: Without landing clearance you must go around before touching the runway.

steps.text: At about 500 ft above the ground, turn the autopilot off: press AP1.
steps.why: Leave the autothrust on: that is common on the Airbus, then you do not worry about thrust and speed.

steps.text: Fly the PAPI: two white and two red lights. Correct carefully if you see 3 or 4 white (too high) or 3 or 4 red (too low).
steps.why: Small sidestick inputs are enough. Aim at the middle of the touchdown zone, and keep the centre line under you.

steps.text: At the threshold (about 50 ft) look to the end of the runway. At about 30 ft pull the sidestick back carefully to flare, a few degrees of pitch.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (4. Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 71 (sections: Flare; At Touchdown; At 70 knots; At Taxi Speed) (Flare)
steps.why: Too much flare floats down the runway, too little lands hard. Do not push the stick forward once flared.

steps.text: At about 10 to 20 ft pull the thrust levers to idle (the aircraft calls RETARD) so you are at idle thrust before touchdown.
steps.why: The autopilot disconnects when the thrust levers go to IDLE (SOP).

steps.text: At touchdown of the main gear pull the thrust levers into reverse.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (4. Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 72 (sections: Flare; At Touchdown; At 70 knots; At Taxi Speed; Before 20 Knots; At 350 feet RA) (At Touchdown)
steps.why: The speed brakes deploy by themselves because they are armed. Lower the nose gear gently and hold the centre line with the rudder. The upper ECAM shows REV and the lower ECAM shows the spoilers. The autobrake annunciators light.

steps.text: At about 60 kt (the SOP says 70 kt) put the thrust levers back to idle.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (4. Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 72 (sections: Flare; At Touchdown; At 70 knots; At Taxi Speed; Before 20 Knots; At 350 feet RA) (At 70 knots)
steps.why: Keeping a high reverse thrust may stall an engine because of an excessive EGT. Stow the reversers at taxi speed.

steps.text: At about 40 kt brake by hand to release the autobrake.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/landing/ (4. Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 73 (sections: Before 20 Knots; At 350 feet RA; At 40 feet RA; At 30 feet RA; At 10 feet RA; At Touchdown) (Before 20 Knots)
steps.why: The SOP says to disengage the autobrake before 20 kt.

ld_auto.title: Autoland
ld_auto.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/flight-guidance/autoland/ (Autoland How-To, Flow From 1000ft); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 73 (sections: Before 20 Knots; At 350 feet RA; At 40 feet RA; At 30 feet RA; At 10 feet RA; At Touchdown)

steps.text: Check the conditions first: ILS CAT II/III runway, crosswind max 20 kt, headwind max 30 kt, tailwind max 10 kt, glide slope between -2.5 and -3.25 degrees, airport below 9200 ft, weight not below 44 000 kg and not above the maximum landing weight.
steps.why: Autoland is not a replacement for learning to land manually.
steps.warn: If CAT1 shows on the FMA, autoland is not authorized. If low visibility procedures are not enforced, the runway must be considered CAT I.

steps.text: Follow the ILS approach, but engage AP2 as well when you arm APPR, and do not disengage the autopilot for landing.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/flight-guidance/autoland/ (ILS Approach); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 61 (sections: Descent Preparation; Initial/Intermediate Approach; Glide Interception from Above; Final Approach; At 350 ft RA)

steps.text: At 1000 ft check you are configured (gear down, flaps 3 or FULL, VAPP, autobrake armed, spoilers armed, LDG memo no blue).
Before 400 ft check the FMA shows LAND in green (LOC and G/S must be engaged, not still capturing). At 350 ft check the ILS course on the PFD.
steps.warn: No LAND at 350 ft: go around, or land manually if you see the runway (CAT II, at or above 80 ft).

steps.text: At 40 ft FLARE must show on the FMA. At 30 ft THRUST IDLE shows. At 10 ft when the aircraft calls RETARD, move the thrust levers to idle.
steps.warn: No FLARE at 40 ft: go around.

steps.text: At touchdown ROLL OUT shows. Pull the thrust levers into reverse (idle or max), watch the ground spoilers and reversers, keep the centre line with the rudder.
steps.warn: No ROLL OUT: disconnect the autopilot and follow the centre line by hand.

steps.text: At 70 kt reverse idle. Before 20 kt brake by hand to deactivate the autobrake. At taxi speed thrust levers idle and disengage the autopilots.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/flight-guidance/autoland/ (Flow From 1000ft); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 74 (sections: At 70 knots; Before 20 Knots; End or Roll Out)

steps.text: If the red autoland warning light shows below 200 ft: go around.
steps.why: It comes on with both APs lost, a big difference between the radio altimeters, loss of LOC or G/S, or too far off the beam.

steps.text: Look for the next runway exit and slow down to about 15 kt before you start turning off.
Keep rolling until the whole aircraft has passed the runway entry marker.
Stop the aircraft on the taxiway and tell ATC you have vacated, if they have not called you yet.
steps.why: You are alone in the simulator, so you can stop and do the after landing items one after the other.

ld_done.title: Landed
ld_done.text: You have vacated the runway. Next: the topic 'After landing and shutdown'.

ga_air.title: Where is the aircraft?
ga_air.text: Is the aircraft in the air?

ga_ground.title: On the ground
ga_ground.text: A go-around is a flight procedure. On the ground, a rejected take-off has its own topic.

ga_do.title: Go-around
ga_do.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/flight-guidance/autoland/ (Go-Around); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 75-76 (sections: At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude; At Go Around Acceleration Altitude) (Go Around With FD)

steps.text: At the same time: push the thrust levers to TOGA, rotate towards 15 degrees pitch up, and announce 'Go around'.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/flight-guidance/autoland/ (Go-Around); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 75 (sections: At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude; At Go Around Acceleration Altitude)
steps.why: TOGA gives SRS GA mode. You can then move the levers to FLX/MCT to get GA SOFT. When you get a positive rate of climb, follow the SRS flight director.

steps.text: Retract one step of flaps.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 75 (sections: At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude; At Go Around Acceleration Altitude) (Go Around With FD)

steps.text: Check the FMA: MAN GA SOFT or MAN TOGA, SRS, GA TRK or NAV, A/THR. If MAN GA SOFT or MAN TOGA is not shown, set the thrust levers to TOGA.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/flight-guidance/autoland/ (Go-Around); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 75 (sections: At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude; At Go Around Acceleration Altitude)

steps.text: With a positive climb, retract the landing gear.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 75 (sections: At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude; At Go Around Acceleration Altitude) (Go Around With FD)

steps.text: Use NAV or HDG as required, and engage the autopilot as required.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 75 (sections: At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude; At Go Around Acceleration Altitude) (Go Around With FD)

steps.text: At the go-around thrust reduction altitude set the thrust levers to CL.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 75 (sections: At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude; At Go Around Acceleration Altitude) (At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude)

steps.text: At the acceleration altitude check the target speed goes to green dot. If not, verify the ALT knob and pull it.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 76 (sections: At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude; At Go Around Acceleration Altitude) (At Go Around Acceleration Altitude)

steps.text: At F speed select flaps 1; at S speed select flaps 0, disarm the ground spoilers, and turn the NOSE and RWY TURN OFF lights OFF.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 76 (sections: At Go Around Thrust Reduction Altitude; At Go Around Acceleration Altitude)
steps.why: Then complete the AFTER TAKEOFF checklist. Plan a new approach or divert.

ga_done.title: Go-around flown
ga_done.text: Decide with ATC: a new approach (topic 'Descent and approach') or a diversion (topic 'Change the flight plan').

sd_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
sd_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?

sd_air.title: Still flying
sd_air.text: Use the topics 'Descent and approach' and 'Landing' first.

sd_eng.title: Where in the process?
sd_eng.text: What state is the aircraft in?

choices.label: Just vacated the runway, engines running
Engines off, passengers still on board / cleaning
Everyone has left, I want to secure the aircraft

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

sd_afterland.title: After landing
sd_afterland.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/after-landing/ (1. After Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 78 (sections: After Landing; Exterior lights)

steps.text: Set the radio to the ground frequency from the chart or ATC.
Disarm the ground spoilers: push the speed brake lever down.
Set the ENG mode selector to NORM if it is at IGN/START.
Retract the flaps to 0.
steps.why: If the approach was in icing conditions, wait until the ground crew confirms the flaps and slats are free of ice (SOP).

steps.text: Set the TCAS to STBY.
Set the weather radar and the PWS to OFF.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/after-landing/ (1. After Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 78 (sections: After Landing; Exterior lights)
steps.why: The SOP says so to avoid any risk of radiating the ground crew.

steps.text: Start the APU: press APU MASTER SW, then START.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/after-landing/ (1. After Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 78 (sections: After Landing; Exterior lights)
steps.why: Long use of the APU may cause a fuel imbalance.

steps.text: Turn the anti-ice off if you do not need it.
Set the NOSE light to TAXI and the RWY TURN OFF light to ON.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/after-landing/ (1. After Landing, Set your exterior lights)

steps.text: Set the STROBE switch to AUTO (or OFF), but keep the strobes ON while crossing a runway until you have vacated it.
Retract the LAND lights (or turn them off).
If you get a HOT BRAKES warning on the ECAM, turn the brake fan on.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/after-landing/ (1. After Landing); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 79 (sections: After Landing; Exterior lights)
steps.why: The SOP recommends delaying the brake fans until 5 minutes after landing.

steps.text: Run the AFTER LANDING checklist.
steps.why: Item: RADAR & PRED W/S OFF.

sd_taxi.title: Taxi to the gate
sd_taxi.text: Follow the ATC taxi instructions with your chart and read the Taxi section of 'Taxi'. Only cross a runway with clear permission and read back; turn the STROBE lights ON while crossing. When you turn into the gate, turn off the NOSE light and the RWY TURN OFF lights so you do not blind the ground crew, but only if there is enough light to park safely.

sd_parking.title: Parking at the gate
sd_parking.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/powering-down/ (1. Parking at the Gate); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 80-81 (sections: Parking)

steps.text: Set the parking brake.
steps.why: The SOP advises against it if one brake is above 500 degC (350 degC with the brake fan on).

steps.text: Turn the NOSE and RWY TURN OFF lights off (if you did not already).
Turn the APU BLEED ON before you shut down the engines.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/powering-down/ (1. Parking at the Gate); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 80 (sections: Parking)
steps.why: The SOP says this minimises engine exhaust smells in the air conditioning. The APU must be available.

steps.text: Shut down the engines: set the ENG 1 and ENG 2 master switches to OFF.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/powering-down/ (1. Parking at the Gate); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 81 (sections: Parking)
steps.why: The SOP recommends running at or near idle for 3 minutes after high thrust before the shutdown. Taxi and idle reverse are not high thrust.

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

steps.text: Wait until N1 is below 5 %.
Turn the SEAT BELTS sign off.
Turn the BEACON light off. Leave NAV & LOGO on while the aircraft has power; the strobes can stay on AUTO.
Run the PARKING checklist.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/powering-down/ (1. Parking at the Gate); FBW A32NX Checklist.pdf
steps.why: Items: PARK BRK or CHOCKS set, ENGINES off, WINGS LIGHT off, FUEL PUMPS off, YELLOW ELEC PUMP off.

steps.text: If external power is available and connected by the ground crew, press EXT PWR.
steps.why: Turning off the APU depends on the turn-around time. For a shutdown, do it after the passengers have left, to keep the cabin air flowing.

sd_pax.title: Passengers and baggage
sd_pax.text: In the simulator you trigger these yourself with the flyPad ground functions (open it with Ctrl+0): connect the jetway (PAX) and call the baggage truck. Real turnarounds take a while, and you cannot shut the aircraft down before everyone has left. For a turnaround you would not switch off some systems and would start the preparation again; the Beginner Guide gives no turnaround list.
sd_pax.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/powering-down/ (2. Disembarking Passengers and Baggage, Preface); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/ (Ground Service)

sd_secure_q.title: Next
sd_secure_q.text: Do you want to secure the aircraft (back to cold and dark) now?

choices.label: No, I am done or doing a turnaround

sd_secure.title: Securing the aircraft
sd_secure.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/powering-down/ (3. Securing the Aircraft); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 82-84 (sections: Parking Brake; Oxygen Crew Supply; ADIRS; Exterior Lights; Maintenance Bus; APU)

steps.text: Check the passengers and cargo are gone and the cabin is clean.
Turn all the fuel pumps off.

check.code: (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:2, Bool) (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:3, Bool) + (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:5, Bool) + (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:6, Bool) +

steps.text: Set the three ADIRS selectors to OFF.
Turn the crew oxygen supply off.
Turn the APU BLEED off.
Set the EMER EXIT LT switch and the NO SMOKING switch to OFF.
Optional (airline SOP): reset the air conditioning, lighting and screen brightness.
Turn the APU MASTER off.
steps.why: The APU can still show AVAIL for a few minutes if it supplied bleed air shortly before, because it needs to cool down.

steps.text: Wait 2 minutes for the APU flap door to close.
steps.why: Closing the door needs APU or external power.

steps.text: Turn the EXT PWR button off if it was on.
Turn the NAV & LOGO lights off.
steps.why: The aircraft no longer has power.

steps.text: Turn BAT 1 and BAT 2 off.
steps.why: The SOP keeps the parking brake ON to reduce hydraulic leaks. The aircraft is now cold and dark.

sd_done.title: Done
sd_done.text: The aircraft is parked. After the Securing step it is back in a cold and dark state.

cf_q.title: Change the flight plan
cf_q.text: What do you want to do?

choices.label: Add a waypoint or a direct leg
Deal with a discontinuity or delete a waypoint

cf_q.help: Changes from a LAT REV page create a temporary flight plan (yellow TMPY on the F-PLN page) that you must insert.

cf_wpt.title: Add a waypoint or a direct leg
cf_wpt.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/f-pln/ (LAT REV Page Elements, NEXT WPT); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (DCT Before a Waypoint)

steps.text: On the F-PLN page press the LSK next to the waypoint after which the new waypoint goes.
steps.why: This opens the LAT REV page for that waypoint.

steps.text: Type the new waypoint and press LSK3R (NEXT WPT).
steps.why: If the waypoint is already later in the flight plan, all the waypoints in between are removed. If it is a new waypoint, a discontinuity is created after it.

steps.text: If the F-PLN page shows TMPY (temporary flight plan), press INSERT* (LSK6R) to activate it.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/f-pln/ (F-PLN Page Elements, Lateral Revision Pages); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (Enroute Flight Plan)

steps.text: Find the hold on the chart: fix, inbound course, turn direction, leg length (time or distance), maximum speed.
steps.why: If the chart gives no other value, the FMS uses its standards (next step).

steps.text: On the F-PLN page press the LSK next to the hold waypoint, then select HOLD (LSK3L).
steps.why: The page is called COMPUTED HOLD. The FMS computed it, and you can overwrite it.

steps.text: Type the inbound course and enter it. Set the turn direction if it is not right (the default is right).
steps.why: Large characters mean the value is entered by you. REVERT TO COMPUTED restores the computed values.

steps.text: Type the leg length: /10 for 10 NM or 1.5 for 1.5 minutes, then press LSK3 (TIME/DIST).
steps.why: Default leg time: 1 minute at or below 14 000 ft, 1.5 minutes above. Default speed is the lowest of max endurance, the ICAO limit (230 kt below 14 000 ft, 240 up to 20 000, 265 up to 34 000, M 0.83 above), a speed constraint or the speed limit.

steps.text: Press INSERT (LSK6R).
steps.why: The hold shows on the ND with a white curved arrow. The A320 flies the right entry pattern by itself. If the speed is selected, SET HOLD SPEED asks you to set the hold speed or engage managed speed.

steps.text: To leave the hold: press IMM EXIT* on the F-PLN page, or do a DIR TO.
steps.why: The aircraft shortens the hold, flies to the fix and continues with the flight plan. RESUME HOLD brings the hold back before the fix.

cf_disco.title: Discontinuities and deleted waypoints
cf_disco.text: A discontinuity is a break in the flight plan. Between SID and route, or between STAR and approach, it is normal and the NAV mode reverts to HDG: follow ATC vectors or use DIR TO to the next waypoint. After a MANUAL leg (a constant heading or track without end point) the discontinuity cannot and should not be deleted: use selected HDG or DIR TO to reach the approach. If you delete a waypoint yourself, a discontinuity is left in its place and you may delete that one to join the route again (CLR). Do not clear a discontinuity between SID and route unless you understand the routing: narrow turns and incompatible leg types can result. A flight plan that ends in a discontinuity is the usual reason why the aircraft does not follow the route.
cf_disco.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/flight-planning/disco/ (What are Discontinuities, Discontinuities After Deleting Waypoints, Special Cases); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Aircraft Not Following Flight Plan Route)

cf_arr.title: Change the runway, STAR or approach
cf_arr.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/f-pln/ (ARRIVAL Page); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (Planning the Arrival); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 51-52 (sections: Descent Preparation)

steps.text: On the F-PLN page press the LSK next to the destination airport, then select ARRIVAL (LSK1R).
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (Planning the Arrival); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/f-pln/ (LAT REV Page Elements, ARRIVAL)

steps.text: Select the approach (with its runway), then the STAR, then the VIA, then a transition if offered.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (Planning the Arrival); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 52 (sections: Descent Preparation)

steps.text: Press INSERT* (LSK6R) and scroll through the flight plan to check it.
steps.why: A discontinuity between the STAR and the approach is normal. Check it against the chart and the restrictions.

steps.text: Go to PERF, APPR and check the destination data and the minimums again.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 52 (sections: Descent Preparation) (PERF APPR page); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/perf/ (APPROACH, BARO)
steps.why: A change of runway or approach type erases the entered minimum. Also check the ILS on RAD NAV.

cf_dest.title: Divert: new destination or alternate
cf_dest.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/f-pln/ (LAT REV Page Elements: NEW DEST, ENABLE ALTN)

steps.text: On the F-PLN page press the LSK next to a waypoint of the route, then select NEW DEST (LSK4R) and type the new airport.
steps.why: It creates a temporary flight plan direct to the new destination, removes the waypoints between and leaves a discontinuity. Follow the discontinuity advice in 'Discontinuities and deleted waypoints'.

steps.text: Insert the temporary flight plan (INSERT*), then select the arrival with ARRIVAL as in 'Change runway, STAR or approach'.
Enter the weather and approach data on PERF, APPR for the new airport, and check RAD NAV.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 52 (sections: Descent Preparation) (PERF APPR page, RAD NAV page)

steps.text: To use the planned alternate instead, select ENABLE ALTN (LSK4L) on a LAT REV page.
steps.why: It creates a temporary flight plan. The list of alternates (ALTN, LSK5L) does not work in the A32NX.

cf_sec.title: Secondary flight plan
cf_sec.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/sec-fpln/ (Engine-out Departure Procedure, Activating the Secondary Flight Plan)

steps.text: Press SEC F-PLN on the MCDU and select COPY ACTIVE to copy the active flight plan.
steps.warn: The page says this feature is available on the Development version, and that predictions for the secondary flight plan are not yet computed. The briefing page for SEC F-PLN says it was not implemented.

steps.text: Change the secondary plan as needed (runway, SID, route, arrival). It does not create a temporary flight plan.
steps.why: The SOP recommends the secondary flight plan for a runway change, an immediate return or an emergency landing (SOP p.22).

steps.text: When you need it, select ACTIVATE SEC on the SEC F-PLN page. SWAP ACTIVE swaps the two plans.
steps.why: ACTIVATE SEC appears only if both plans have the same active leg or the aircraft is in HDG mode. After activation, do a direct-to to re-engage NAV.

cf_done.title: Flight plan changed
cf_done.text: Check the new route on the ND (PLAN mode) and the FMA. For the speed, altitude or heading see 'FCU and autopilot'.

ai_q.title: Anti-ice and rain
ai_q.help: Icing conditions: outside air temperature (on the ground and after take-off) or total air temperature (in flight) at or below 10 degC with visible moisture (cloud, fog of 1600 m / 1 sm or less, rain, snow, sleet, ice crystals). On the ground also when at or below 10 degC and surface snow, standing water or slush can be ingested by the engines.

ai_gnd.title: Anti-ice on the ground
ai_gnd.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/ice-rain-protection/ (Usage of the Ice and Rain Protection System, Other Procedures); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 32 (sections: Engine Mode; APU Bleed; Anti-Ice; APU; Ground Spoilers; Rudder Trim)

steps.text: Turn the engine anti-ice ON for all ground operations where icing conditions exist or are expected.
steps.why: It raises the idle N1: take care when taxiing. The SOP allows an engine de-icing run-up if the surface and environment allow: parking brake ON, then engines to at least 50 % N1 for 5 seconds.

check.code: (A:ENG ANTI ICE:1, Bool) (A:ENG ANTI ICE:2, Bool) +

steps.text: Do not use the wing anti-ice on the ground except for the 30 second test.
While taxiing in icing conditions keep the flaps retracted until the runway holding point.
steps.why: It stops contamination of the flap and slat mechanism.

steps.text: Leave the PROBE/WINDOW HEAT button on AUTO.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/ice-rain-protection/ (PROBE/WINDOW HEAT pushbutton); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 18 (sections: Signs; Probe / Window Heat; Cabin Pressure; Air Conditioning; Electrical; Fuel) (Probe / Window Heat)
steps.why: Windows and probes (except the TAT probes) are heated automatically when at least one engine is running.

steps.text: If it rains, set the wipers to SLOW or FAST. Never use them on a dry windshield.

ai_air.title: Anti-ice in flight
ai_air.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/ice-rain-protection/ (Usage of the Ice and Rain Protection System); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 44-45 (sections: After Takeoff)

steps.text: Turn the engine anti-ice ON when icing conditions exist or are expected, except in climb or cruise when the SAT is below -40 degC.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-advanced-guides/ice-rain-protection/ (ENG 1 + 2 Anti-Ice pushbuttons); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 44 (sections: After Takeoff)
steps.why: The SOP for the descent recommends engine anti-ice ON even if the SAT is below -40 degC, for a better protection against flame-out.

check.code: (A:ENG ANTI ICE:1, Bool) (A:ENG ANTI ICE:2, Bool) +

steps.text: Turn the wing anti-ice ON when there is visible airframe icing on the visual ice indicator or the wipers.
steps.why: Wing anti-ice reduces the N1 limit. Turn it OFF for landing unless the icing is severe (SOP). The anti-ice reduces the descent path angle: you can compensate with more descent speed or up to half speed brakes.

steps.text: Leave the PROBE/WINDOW HEAT button on AUTO: windows and probes are heated automatically in flight.
For the approach: delay the flap retraction after landing until the ground crew confirms the flaps and slats are free of ice.

ai_done.title: Known limit of the simulator
ai_done.text: There is no real anti-ice in MSFS (Asobo has no plans to add it), so the anti-ice systems work as de-ice systems: ice can still build up when they are on, and it melts fairly quickly. You can lose airspeed information when you first enter severe icing conditions. No workaround exists; flights are not much affected.

rx_q.title: Radios and transponder
rx_q.text: What do you want to do?

steps.text: On the radio management panel (RMP), press the VHF key of the radio you want (the key lights green).
steps.why: The ACTIVE window then shows the current frequency, the STBY/CRS window the standby frequency. Tip: use VHF 1 for ATC and emergency frequencies, VHF 2 for the ATIS (SOP).

steps.text: Turn the frequency selector knobs to set the standby frequency.
Press the transfer key to make it the active frequency.
steps.why: It swaps the active and standby frequencies.

steps.text: Double press CLR to clear the code, then type the four-digit code ATC gave you.
steps.why: As long as the four digits are not complete the previous code remains.

steps.text: Set the mode: STBY on the ground until take-off, AUTO or ON for take-off and flight.
steps.why: AUTO on the ground only answers in mode S; in flight the selected transponder works. Only XPDR 1 is available in this simulator.

steps.text: Set ALT RPTG to ON.
steps.why: With ALT RPTG off, there is no altitude data, and the upper ECAM shows TCAS STBY.

steps.text: When ATC asks you to ident, press the IDENT button.
Set the TCAS mode to TA/RA in normal flight (TA only for degraded performance, gear extended or parallel runways).
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/atc-tcas/ (TCAS Mode); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 44 (sections: After Takeoff)

steps.text: Set the TCAS traffic display: ALL or ABV for take-off; THRT, ALL, ABV or BLW as needed.

fs_q.title: Fuel and systems
fs_q.text: What do you want to do?

choices.label: Monitor fuel and systems in flight

fs_load.title: Load fuel and passengers
fs_load.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/ground/ (Fuel Page, Payload Page); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/ (Loading Fuel and Weight)

steps.text: On the flyPad open Ground, Fuel. Type the fuel quantity (or import it from SimBrief) and press the play button.
steps.why: The MSFS fuel window is blocked. If the play button is missing or disabled, GSX synchronisation is probably on (see Troubleshooting). Fuel on board is saved after the flight and used the next time with the same registration.

steps.text: Open the Payload page, enter the passengers or the zero fuel weight and press Boarding.
steps.why: Weight limits (kg): empty 42 500, max zero fuel 64 300, max take-off 79 000, max landing 67 400; max fuel 19 046. The aircraft does not stop you from overloading in manual loading.
steps.warn: MLW and MTOW are not checked when you load by hand.

steps.text: Then enter the ZFW and the block fuel on the MCDU INIT B page (see 'Flight plan and performance').

fs_pumps.title: Fuel pumps and centre tank
fs_pumps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 18 (sections: Signs; Probe / Window Heat; Cabin Pressure; Air Conditioning; Electrical; Fuel) (Fuel); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/fuel/

steps.text: Keep the wing tank pumps ON. They stay on during the flight.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/ovhd/fuel/ (Description, L + R TK PUMPS); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Hydraulic and Fuel Section)
steps.why: A FAULT light and an ECAM caution show when the pressure drops while the pump is not OFF.

steps.text: If the centre tank has less than 200 kg (440 lb) for the flight: set MODE SEL to MAN and the centre tank pumps OFF. Otherwise verify MODE SEL is on AUTO.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 18 (sections: Signs; Probe / Window Heat; Cabin Pressure; Air Conditioning; Electrical; Fuel) (Fuel)
steps.why: Tanks empty in this order: centre tank, inner tanks (down to 750 kg), then the outer tanks transfer into the inner tanks. The A320neo has jet pumps in the centre tank: you only control the valves.

steps.text: If the outer tank fuel does not transfer, add fuel on the ground to be above the transfer trigger point of 239 gallons.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Unexpected Out of Fuel - No Fuel Transfer From Outer Tanks)
steps.why: The sim can miss the trigger point, or the fuel on board at the start is below it.

fs_watch.title: Monitor fuel and systems
fs_watch.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 49 (sections: Cruise) (Cruise)

steps.text: Review the ECAM system pages regularly: ENG, BLEED, ELEC, HYD, FUEL, COND, F/CTL, DOOR.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 49 (sections: Cruise)

steps.text: Every 30 minutes compare the fuel on board and the MCDU fuel prediction with the flight plan.
steps.source: FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 49 (sections: Cruise) (Flight Progress)
steps.why: The fuel on board plus the fuel used should match the fuel at departure.

steps.text: Add more fuel than the MCDU computes when you plan fuel with the MCDU, especially for longer flights.
steps.why: The fuel prediction is not accurate until the fuel planning feature has been updated.

ts_start.title: What is the problem?

choices.label: Displays are black, no power, lights act strange
Engines will not start or shut down by themselves
Autopilot, autothrust or flight mode problems
Aircraft will not move, steer or brake well
Switches, knobs, mouse or controls do not respond
Loading, invisible aircraft, freezes, FPS, crashes

ts_start.help: Most reported problems are caused by conflicts with other add-ons and liveries. If a fix here does not help, go through the general troubleshooting steps at the end.

ts_power_q.title: Power
ts_power_q.text: Are the batteries switched on (BAT 1 and BAT 2 AUTO)?

steps.text: Set BAT 1 and BAT 2 to AUTO (no white OFF light).
steps.why: Batteries power only a small part of the aircraft. For the rest, external power, the APU or a running engine is required.

ts_ac_q.title: AC power
ts_ac_q.text: Is AC bus 1 powered (external power, APU or engine generator supplies the aircraft)?

steps.text: If the green AVAIL light shows on EXT PWR, press the EXT PWR button.
steps.why: Some gates have no ground power. That is realistic, not a bug. The flyPad Ground page has 'Connect External Power'.

steps.text: Otherwise start the APU: MASTER SW, then START (see 'External power, APU and batteries').
Wait about 50 seconds for the flight warning system to start.
steps.why: The FWS FWC 1+2 FAULT message shows during the start-up and then disappears.

ts_black.title: Power is on, but the cockpit is wrong
ts_black.text: If systems like the electrics are broken, the displays stay black, the cockpit layout is broken, or lights and displays are partly on and partly off, FlyByWire lists these fixes: 1) Test with only the A32NX add-on in the Community folder: rename the Community folder to Community.old, create an empty one and reinstall the A32NX with the FlyByWire Installer. This is called the most important troubleshooting step. 2) Do a clean install. 3) Remove an old Marketplace installation (look for old 'flybywire' versions in the Content Manager, uninstall them and restart the sim). 4) Enable Windows UTF-8 support (Region, Administrative, Change system locale, tick 'Beta: Use UTF-8'). 5) Use the latest version of MSFS. Add-ons known to break lights or displays: lights add-ons (for example 'New Light'), the LVFR A321neo compatibility mod, co-pilot add-ons, third-party interior texture packs, the Weather Radar mod. These instructions are written for Windows.
ts_black.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Broken Systems, Black Screens; Cockpit Lights and Display Are Erratically On; Incompatible and Problematic Add-ons/Mods); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/

choices.label: The engines shut down by themselves

ts_nostart.title: The engine will not start
ts_nostart.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Ctrl+E - Engine Start Unsupported); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Engine Start); FBW A32NX SOP.pdf, printed page 29 (sections: Automatic Engine Start)

steps.text: Check that there is fuel on board and that the fuel pumps are ON.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Unexpected Engines Shut Down); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/starting-the-aircraft/ (Hydraulic and Fuel Section)
steps.why: Forgetting to load fuel is a common cause. Fuel is loaded only with the flyPad.

check.code: (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:2, Bool) (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:3, Bool) + (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:5, Bool) + (A:FUELSYSTEM PUMP SWITCH:6, Bool) +

steps.text: Check the APU is available (AVAIL light).
steps.why: You need at least the APU AVAIL, the APU bleed ON and the fuel pumps ON for a normal engine start.

steps.text: Check the APU BLEED button is ON.
Set the ENG mode selector to IGN/START, then the master switch to ON.
Do not use the Ctrl+E auto-start shortcut: it does not work with this aircraft.
steps.why: The A32NX needs the normal procedure. The SOP also advises waiting until all the amber crosses and messages have gone from the upper ECAM before the master switch.

steps.text: If you use a Thrustmaster TCA throttle: remove the 'Toggle Engine 1/2 Fuel Valve' mappings from the TCA buttons and keep the 'Set Engine 1/2 Fuel Valve' ones.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Can't Start Engines When Using TCA Throttle)
steps.why: The MSFS default TCA mapping is wrong for this aircraft.

steps.text: Turn off all the MSFS assistance and AI features.
steps.why: They caused engines turning off in flight or after take-off.

ts_shut.title: Engines shut down by themselves
ts_shut.text: FlyByWire lists two usual causes: a conflicting controller or keyboard mapping that triggers the engine shutdown (for example an 'Auto Start Engine' mapping, or buttons also bound to the gear or flaps), and forgetting to fuel the aircraft. Remove the conflicting mapping and follow the fuelling procedure in the flyPad (Ground, Fuel). Also turn off the MSFS assistance features; with them on, engines turned off in flight or after take-off.
ts_shut.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Unexpected Engines Shut Down); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/ (Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features)

choices.label: LVR CLB keeps flashing / autothrust does not hold the speed / FLX or TOGA does not engage
SRS or RWY mode does not engage on take-off
LAND mode or autoland does not work

steps.text: Check your controllers do not send unwanted input. Increase the deadzone in the MSFS controller settings: start at 20 % and increase until it stops.
steps.why: This is one of the most common causes. Settings, Controls, select the device, then the sensitivity button on the top left.

steps.text: Turn off the MSFS assistance features.
Check your frame rate. The custom autopilot needs a stable 17 fps at least.
steps.why: With time compression, you need about 30 fps at 2x and about 45 fps at 4x.

steps.text: Remember the protections disconnect the autopilot: high speed (VMO + 15 kt or MMO + 0.04), and high angle of attack including alpha floor.
steps.why: Using the pitch trim wheel in flight also disconnects the autopilot (briefing page, Thrust Lever and Pitch Trim).

ts_athr.title: Autothrust and thrust lever problems
ts_athr.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/autopilot-fbw/ (Typical Issues and How to Solve Them); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/; https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/flight-deck/pedestal/thrust-pitch-trim/

steps.text: Calibrate the throttle with the flyPad throttle configuration, following the Throttle Calibration guide step by step.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/autopilot-fbw/ (FMA keeps blinking with message LVR CLB); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/throttle-calibration/
steps.why: A flashing LVR CLB, FLX / TOGA not engaging, or the A/THR not holding the speed usually mean the detents are not set up properly. Make the detents wide enough (hardware is inexact, especially on the Thrustmaster TCA) and leave at least as much range between detents. Check the values in the EFB, not the animation of the levers.

steps.text: Check the thrust levers are in the CL detent, the A/THR is active, and the FMA mode is SPEED or MACH.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/autopilot-fbw/ (Autothrust does not hold target speed in manual flight)
steps.why: In manual flight in CLB, OP CLB, DES or OP DES the A/THR only applies THR CLB or THR IDLE: you control the speed with the pitch. To change it, engage V/S or FPA, or switch both flight directors off (this forces SPEED mode).

steps.text: If the A/THR is gone for the whole flight: it happens when the red A/THR disconnect button is held for more than 15 seconds.
steps.why: All A/THR functions incl. ALPHA FLOOR are lost and can only be recovered at the next FMGC power-up on the ground.

steps.text: Turn off the MSFS assistance features.
steps.why: A/THR failing to arm or activate was a symptom.

ts_srs.title: SRS or RWY does not engage on take-off
ts_srs.text: SRS needs at least V2 entered on the PERF TAKE OFF page. It also engages only if the thrust lever detents are set up properly (TOGA if no FLEX temperature is set; FLX/MCT or TOGA if one is set), the aircraft has been at least 30 seconds on the ground, and the flaps are at least in 1+F. RWY needs a valid LOC signal: there is no auto-tune of the localizer for take-off, so enter the frequency by hand on RAD NAV; the LOC deviation must be less than half a dot, the difference between aircraft heading and LOC bearing less than 20 degrees, at least 30 seconds on the ground, and flaps at least 1+F. If LVR CLB flashes immediately after lift-off, check the thrust reduction and acceleration altitudes on the PERF page.
ts_srs.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/autopilot-fbw/ (SRS does not engage on take-off; RWY does not engage on take-off; LVR CLB flashes immediately after lift-off)

ts_land.title: LAND mode or autoland does not work
ts_land.text: LAND needs LOC and G/S engaged before reaching 400 ft radio altitude. If one of them is still capturing (LOC* or G/S*), go around or land manually. Autoland also depends on the quality of the runway data in the sim: LOC alignment and availability down to 0 ft and during roll-out, G/S accuracy and availability down to 50 ft, and stable ground ahead of the threshold from 200 ft. On many runways the LOC is lost during ROLL OUT; then disengage the autopilot and finish the roll-out by hand. If the red autoland warning light comes on, go around.
ts_land.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/autopilot-fbw/ (LAND mode does not engage; Autoland does not perform as expected)

ts_osc.title: The autopilot oscillates
ts_osc.text: Make sure you have enough frames per second (at least a stable 17 fps). With time compression the requirement grows: about 30 fps at 2x and about 45 fps at 4x; heavy turbulence may need less. Oscillation in flight or on approach: also remove any mod or add-on that changes the flight model or physics, which are not supported.
ts_osc.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/autopilot-fbw/ (Autopilot is oscillating; Autopilot oscillates when using time compression; Climb performance is not satisfying)

choices.label: INIT REQUEST is missing / the SimBrief import fails
NOT IN DATABASE, AWY/WPT MISMATCH, NOT ALLOWED
The aircraft does not follow the route
SRS is missing on take-off, speeds amber
Pause appears when I type on the MCDU or flyPad

ts_initreq.title: INIT REQUEST missing or import fails
ts_initreq.text: Do not select an arrival airport (or departure and arrival) in the MSFS world map before loading the flight: this fills the FROM/TO field and removes the INIT REQUEST option on INIT A. Reload the flight without an arrival airport. Generate the SimBrief OFP with the 'Detailed Navlog' setting on; without it only the airports may be imported. SimBrief or Navigraph must be linked in the flyPad (Settings, 3rd Party Options). RWY, SID, STAR and approach are never imported: add them by hand. An outdated AIRAC cycle can make the import fail.
ts_initreq.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preflight/ (Flight Plan Import, Nav Data); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/simbrief/ (Initialize Flight Plan, Please Enable Detailed Navlog)

ts_navdata.title: NOT IN DATABASE and similar messages
ts_navdata.text: The A32NX uses the sim's nav data. Flight planning tools with an older AIRAC cycle give routes that are no longer valid in the sim: NOT ALLOWED, NOT IN DATABASE and AWY/WPT MISMATCH. Test with the MSFS World Map: if the waypoint, SID or approach is missing there too, it is a general nav data issue. FlyByWire recommends a Navigraph subscription so SimBrief and the sim have the same nav data; if you have it and still get errors, remove and reinstall the navigation data with the Navigraph Data Center. The error can also come from an outdated A32NX (old Marketplace installation).
ts_navdata.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Nav Data Issues); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Remove Old Marketplace Installation); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preflight/ (Nav Data)

ts_route.title: The aircraft does not follow the route
ts_route.text: This is typically caused by flying into a discontinuity, or by an incomplete set-up of the aircraft. Look at the F-PLN page: a discontinuity ahead means the NAV mode reverts to HDG. Fix it with a DIR TO to the next waypoint or selected heading (see the topic 'Change the flight plan'), or clear it only where that is allowed. Check also the FMA: pushing the HDG knob returns to managed NAV only when there is a route ahead.

ts_weight.title: INITIALIZE WEIGHT/CG and CHECK WEIGHT
ts_weight.text: INITIALIZE WEIGHT/CG (amber) appears when the zero fuel weight or the block fuel is not defined after the engine start. Complete the INIT B / INIT FUEL PRED page before starting an engine: ZFW/ZFWCG (press LSK1R twice to take the computed values) and the block fuel (LSK2R). The computed ZFW is only right when the fuel and payload are set in the aircraft and the boarding is complete or in progress. CHECK WEIGHT (amber) appears when the gross weights computed by the flight management computer and the flight augmentation computer disagree by more than 7 tonnes; the A32NX page gives the same limit between the aerodynamic value and the value from the entered ZFW and fuel flow.
ts_weight.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/a32nx/feature-guides/loading-fuel-weight/ (Cold and Dark Startup); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/messages/ (INITIALIZE WEIGHT/CG, CHECK WEIGHT); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (INIT FUEL PRED)

ts_pause.title: Pause appears when typing
ts_pause.text: If the Pause function is mapped to a key other than Esc, that key triggers Pause when you type it into the input fields of the flyPad or the MCDU in keyboard input mode (an MSFS limitation for Coherent driven JavaScript instruments). Map Pause only to the Esc key.
ts_pause.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Incompatible Keyboard Mapping for Pause Function); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/ (Keyboard Mapping for Pause Function)

choices.label: It is hard to steer or brake, the rudder twitches, brakes stick

ts_wont.title: The aircraft will not move
ts_wont.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Unable to Move or Taxi, Disconnect the Tug); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/engine-start-taxi/ (Moving the Aircraft)

steps.text: Release the parking brake.
Look at the upper ECAM. If NW STRG DISC shows and you see no tug, press Shift+P on the keyboard to disconnect the invisible pushback tug.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Unable to Move or Taxi; Disconnect the Tug)
steps.why: An invisible tug can stay attached because the tug picture and the connection get out of sync (an MSFS issue), sometimes triggered by pushback tools. You can also release the tug on the flyPad pushback page.

steps.text: Check that both engines run, and add a little thrust (about 25 to 30 % N1) if the aircraft does not roll.

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

steps.text: If you use a Toolbar Pushback add-on: remove it from the Community folder, or take it off the toolbar after the pushback. Use the flyPad pushback instead.
steps.why: Its intermittent problems: stuck aircraft, unable to taxi or turn the nose wheel, bad performance.

steps.text: Check that your rudder pedals and toe brakes are calibrated and the MSFS assistance features (especially AUTO_RUDDER) are off.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Rudder or Toe Brake Operation Issues); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/ (Deactivate MSFS Assistance Features)
steps.why: Toe brakes that are not calibrated can hold the aircraft back.

ts_hard.title: Hard to steer or brake
ts_hard.text: Brakes getting stuck, twitching rudders or erratic taxiing come from two causes: MSFS assistance settings (especially AUTO_RUDDER) which must be OFF for the A32NX, and a wrong rudder setup. Deactivate the MSFS assistance features (Menu, Assistance Options) and use the recommended rudder settings; the support page shows the settings for the Thrustmaster T.Flight Rudder Pedals as an example. The settings page also lists a racing-pedals configuration (accelerator pedal to RUDDER AXIS RIGHT reversed, clutch pedal to RUDDER AXIS LEFT reversed, both pedals to CENTER RUDDER) and a Nosewheel Tiller Separation if you have an extra axis. Increase your controller deadzone (start at 20 %) if the controller sends unwanted input.
ts_hard.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Rudder or Toe Brake Operation Issues); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Hard To Control the Aircraft during Taxi, TakeOff, or Landing; Setup Your Controller Deadzones); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/ (Rudder/Tiller, Racing Pedals Compatibility)

choices.label: I cannot push or pull knobs, switches act strangely with the mouse
It is hard to click the switches and knobs
Controls freeze while I look around
I lost the mouse after typing in a flyPad field
The flyPad does not work in the external view

ts_knob.title: Cannot push or pull knobs
ts_knob.text: Use the legacy Cockpit Interaction System: Menu, General Options, Accessibility, 'Cockpit Interaction System', set to 'legacy'. With the New system: highlight a control, hold the left mouse button to lock to it, move the mouse left or right (or use the scroll wheel) to turn a knob. To push a knob, lock to it with the left button and click the right button. To pull a knob, hold the left button and click the middle mouse button (this may clash with a middle-button freelook binding).

ts_click.title: Hard to click controls
ts_click.text: Turn off 'Lens Correction' in the MSFS graphics settings: with it on, it is harder to click and move switches, knobs and buttons. Click spots may also seem misaligned.

ts_freeze.title: Controls freeze while looking around
ts_freeze.text: MSFS blocks all other inputs while freelook is used with a mouse button held down. Try setting TOGGLE COCKPIT FREELOOK to your middle mouse button. The Thrustmaster TCA autobrake knob setting is lost if that block lasts more than 1.5 seconds, so do not look around for longer than that.
ts_freeze.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Controls Freeze up While Looking Around); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (TCA Throttle Autobrake Disengages While Looking Around)

ts_mouse.title: Lost the mouse after typing in a flyPad field
ts_mouse.text: Press Ctrl+Z. If it does not help: open a browser, go to localhost:19999, click on any link, go to the Console tab of that page, type Coherent.call('UNFOCUS_INPUT_FIELD') and press Enter.
ts_mouse.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Lost Use of Mouse After Typing in a flyPad Input Field)

ts_ext.title: flyPad in the external view
ts_ext.text: Due to a sim limitation, the flyPad cannot be used in the external view.
ts_ext.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Flypad Can't Be Used in External View)

choices.label: There is no flyPad in the cockpit
The flyPad is white, outdated or missing features
Refuel or boarding buttons are missing or disabled
Doors or ground services on the flyPad are out of sync
I cannot change fuel in the MSFS fuel window
The fuel ran out although I had fuel

ts_efbmiss.title: No flyPad
ts_efbmiss.text: The default Asobo A320 is selected instead of the FlyByWire aircraft. Select 'FlyByWire Simulations A320neo (LEAP)' in the aircraft selector. Liveries for the default A320neo do not work with the A32NX.
ts_efbmiss.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (flyPad EFB Missing in Cockpit); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/faq/ (Where are our planes in-sim?)

ts_efbold.title: Outdated flyPad or systems
ts_efbold.text: Make sure you have the latest version of the add-on (check with the FlyByWire Installer). A white EFB, old versions or a double installation point to an old Marketplace installation: in the Content Manager filter for 'flybywire', uninstall old versions (for example v0.6.1) or duplicates, restart the sim and reinstall with the installer. Then test with only the A32NX in the Community folder and do a clean install.
ts_efbold.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Outdated Systems And Missing Features; Remove Old Marketplace Installation)

ts_gsx.title: Refuel or boarding buttons missing
ts_gsx.text: This happens when GSX Synchronization is on. If you do not use GSX: on the flyPad go to Settings, 3rd Party Options and disable both GSX Synchronization options. If you use GSX, refuelling and boarding run mostly through GSX, with some actions still in the flyPad (see the GSX Integration guide).
ts_gsx.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Refueling/Boarding Buttons Missing/Disabled on EFB Fuel/Payload Page)

ts_sync.title: Ground services out of sync
ts_sync.text: The aircraft cannot read the true state of the ground services, so the flyPad can be out of sync (for example a door is open but its button is grey). Do a hard reset of the flyPad with the hardware power button, or by pressing and holding the software button.
ts_sync.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Ground Services on the flyPad Are Out of Sync)

ts_mfsfuel.title: MSFS fuel window
ts_mfsfuel.text: The MSFS fuel and weights window is blocked in the A32NX: the sliders move, but after 1 to 3 seconds fuel and payload return to their value. Load fuel and payload only with the flyPad (Ground, Fuel and Payload pages). The MSFS fuel truck page is deactivated too.

ts_outfuel.title: Unexpected out of fuel
ts_outfuel.text: The sim sometimes misses the trigger point for the fuel transfer from the outer tanks, or the fuel on board at the start is below it. Before departure add enough fuel to be past the trigger point of 239 gallons, with the flyPad Fuel page.
ts_outfuel.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (Unexpected Out of Fuel - No Fuel Transfer From Outer Tanks)

choices.label: MSFS freezes after Ready To Fly
ADIRS not aligned when starting on the runway or in the air

ts_invis.title: Invisible aircraft
ts_invis.text: The aircraft can be selected but is invisible in the hangar and after the flight starts. Remove the old Marketplace installation: in the Content Manager filter for 'flybywire', uninstall old versions or duplicates, restart the sim, then reinstall the Development version with the FlyByWire Installer.

ts_load.title: Loading never ends
ts_load.text: Wait at least 20 to 30 minutes first: after an aircraft update the sim compiles the WASM files, which takes very long. Otherwise: remove the old Marketplace installation, do a clean install, use the latest MSFS, enable Windows UTF-8 support, and test with only the A32NX in Community.

ts_uni.title: MSFS freezes after Ready To Fly
ts_uni.text: If your Windows user name (not your Xbox gamertag) contains Unicode characters such as e-diaeresis or o-tilde, MSFS may freeze after 'Ready to Fly'. Change the Windows user name to remove them. Also see the UTF-8 setting.

ts_fps.title: Low FPS or stutter
ts_fps.text: Use DX11, not DX12 (DX12 causes massive performance problems for many users). Remove the Toolbar Pushback add-on and the Your Controls add-on if you do not use them. Test with only the A32NX in Community. Set Lens Correction off and Glass Cockpit Refresh Rate to Medium or Low. MSFS also loses FPS in flights longer than about 2 hours (an MSFS forum issue). The custom autopilot needs a stable 17 fps.
ts_fps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Performance Issues / FPS Issues; Do Not Use DX12); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/install/settings/ (Use DX11, Graphics Settings); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (MSFS Performance Degradation In-Flight)

ts_ctd.title: Crash to desktop
ts_ctd.text: CTDs cannot be analysed (MSFS gives no tools or logs). Users had success with: remove everything from the Community folder; enable Windows UTF-8 support; clean install; stop third-party applications connected to MSFS (FSUIPC, YourControls, FS2Crew, GSX, SPAD.neXt); fly without live weather or live traffic; check the Content Manager for missing packages; delete and rebuild the rolling cache and any manual cache; run the game as administrator. Peripherals that disconnect during the flight can also cause a CTD.

ts_adirs.title: ADIRS not aligned after a runway or air start
ts_adirs.text: ADIRS may not be aligned when you spawn anywhere except cold and dark at a gate (an intermittent MSFS initialization timing issue). Workaround: restart the flight. You can also press 'Align ADIRS' in the flyPad Quick Controls (cog wheel in the status bar) to align immediately.
ts_adirs.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-a32nx/ (ADIRS Not Aligned When Starting at Runway or in the Air); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/common/flypados3/index/ (Quick Controls)

steps.text: Read the Known Issues page for your problem first.
steps.why: Most issues users meet are already on that list.

steps.text: Make sure the problem can be reproduced: restart the sim and try the same situation again.
steps.why: Issues that happen only once usually cannot be investigated.

steps.text: Test in a different situation (other airports, route, weather), then with another aircraft, preferably a default MSFS aircraft.
steps.why: If it also happens with other aircraft, it is most likely not an A32NX problem.

steps.text: Remove everything from the Community folder (rename it to Community.old and create an empty one) and do a clean reinstall with the FlyByWire Installer.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/ (2. How to Troubleshoot); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (Test With Only the A32NX or A380X Add-on in Community)
steps.why: More than 90 % of the reported issues are caused by conflicts with other mods and liveries. This is called the most important troubleshooting step.

steps.text: Stop any other third-party software while you test (FSUIPC, SPAD.neXt, YourControls, FS2Crew and so on).
Turn off all MSFS assistance features, enable UTF-8 support (Windows), and use the latest MSFS and the latest aircraft version.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/known-issues/known-issues-common/ (General Troubleshooting Steps, Turn Off All MS Flight Simulator Assistance Features)

steps.text: If it still happens and it is not a known issue, take screenshots or a video and report it on the FlyByWire Discord (#a32nx-support) or GitHub, with the MSFS version, the aircraft version, the Community folder content and a screenshot of the cockpit.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/aircraft/support/ (4. Report Issue on Discord, 5. Report Issue on the A32NX GitHub)

ts_done.title: End of troubleshooting
ts_done.text: If the fix did not help, go back to 'What is the problem?' or follow the general troubleshooting steps.

mc_q.title: Which MCDU page do you need?
mc_q.text: What do you want to know?

choices.label: How the MCDU works: keys, scratchpad, colours, messages
How to type data: formats of waypoints, weights, speeds, frequencies
MCDU MENU, ATSU, AOC (SimBrief, weather, ATIS)

mc_q.help: This is a reference of the MCDU pages as the FlyByWire briefing describes them. The A32NX has only one mirrored MCDU for now. The MCDU has no entry in the control panels of this program, so these steps do not highlight anything: press the keys on the MCDU in the cockpit.

mc_basics.title: How the MCDU works
mc_basics.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/interface/ (General, Scratchpad, Keys, Characters, Colors); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (Understanding the MCDU)

steps.text: The screen has 14 lines of 24 characters. The first line is the title. There are two columns of data fields, 6 rows each.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/interface/ (General, Line Select Keys and Data Fields)

steps.text: Type with the letter and number keys. The text appears in the scratchpad (the last line).
steps.why: The Space key inserts a blank character. The scratchpad also shows the MCDU messages.

steps.text: To enter the text, press the line select key (LSK) next to the field. To call a page, press the LSK next to its prompt or next to the flight plan element.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/interface/ (Line Select Keys and Data Fields); https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-beginner-guide/preparing-mcdu/ (Line Select Key (LSK))
steps.why: LSK names: 1L to 6L for the left keys and 1R to 6R for the right keys, from top to bottom.

steps.text: Scroll with the slew keys: the up and down arrows scroll a page; the left and right arrows go to the next page of a multi-page element.
steps.why: An arrow at the bottom right shows the page can be scrolled; an arrow in the top-right corner shows another page exists.

steps.text: Use the CLR key to correct: press it once to remove the last character; hold it to clear the whole scratchpad.
To erase a data field: press CLR on an empty scratchpad (CLR appears in the scratchpad), then press the LSK next to the field.
The Overfly key makes the aircraft overfly a selected waypoint.

The AIRPORT key shows the flight plan page with the next airport. Pushing it again shows the destination, the alternate (if in the flight plan), the origin (before take-off) and the destination again.

Read the font and colours: large font = your entries and modifiable data; small font = defaulted, computed or non-modifiable data. Blue = modifiable or selectable data and brackets. Green = non-modifiable or active data. Amber = mandatory data (boxes), crew action required, important messages. Magenta = constraints and max altitude. White = titles, comments, arrows, dashes, advisory messages.

Flight plan colours: primary flight plan = green waypoints; temporary flight plan = yellow waypoints; secondary = white; missed approach and alternate (not active) = blue. In the A32NX only the primary flight plan is available.
Messages in the scratchpad are amber (important) or white (advisory). Clear them with CLR. Type 2 messages wait in a queue of at most 5 and show only when nothing else is in the scratchpad.
steps.why: The BRT and DIM keys control the light of the MCDU. The annunciators (FM, IND, RDY, FAIL, MCDU MENU) are not available in the A32NX.

steps.text: Airports: type the four-letter ICAO code, departure and arrival as DEP/ARR (for example EDDM/EDDF), then press LSK1R on INIT A.
Cruise flight level: type the number (for example 240 for FL240) and press LSK6L on INIT A. This also enters the temperature.
Block fuel and weights: block fuel is typed in tonnes (4631 kg is typed 4.7, rounded to the nearest tenth).
steps.why: Press LSK1R once on INIT B to load the computed ZFW/ZFWCG into the scratchpad, and again to enter it.

steps.text: Winds: a trip wind starts with - , H or HD for a headwind, and with + , T or TL for a tailwind. A wind you enter by hand has the format magnetic heading / wind speed / altitude (altitude as a flight level).
Destination QNH: 3 or 4 digits are hPa (1003 = 1003 hPa). 2 digits, or 2 digits, a point and 2 more digits are inches of mercury (29 = 29.00, 29.92 = 29.92).
Minimum on the approach page: BARO holds the DA/MDA; RADIO holds the decision height for CAT II/III (0 to 700 ft). RADIO also accepts NO, NODH or NO DH.
Take-off trim: UP X.X or X.X UP, DN X.X or X.X DN, for example /0.4DN or /1.5UP after the flaps entry. Flaps: type the number, for example 1. FLEX temperature: degrees Celsius.
Altitude constraint on VERT REV: type the altitude; + in front means at or above, - in front means at or below.
Hold leg: type /10 for 10 NM or 1.5 for 1.5 minutes into the TIME/DIST field.
Navigation point (PROG BRG/DIST): an ident (ESSA26 = runway 26 at ESSA), latitude/longitude (5939.1N/01755.1E), place/bearing/distance (ESSA/270/20) or place-bearing/place-bearing (ESSA-270/ESGG-0).
Latitude/longitude format: latitude is 4 digits with one decimal and N or S; longitude is 4 or 5 digits with one decimal and E or W; the two are separated by /. The leading 0 may be left out.
Frequencies and navaids: type the frequency (for example 109.50) or the identifier, not both: both give a FORMAT ERROR. When tuning by hand, prefer the ident unless the navaid is not in the database.

Stored waypoints: type a new unique name into the scratchpad and insert it into the flight plan to open the NEW WAYPOINT page. If you type a latitude/longitude, PBD or PBX point directly on the F-PLN page, the FMS names it LLnn, PBDnn or PBXnn.
Press the INIT key to open INIT A. The horizontal slew keys switch between INIT A and INIT FUEL PRED.

FROM/TO (1R): the departure and arrival airports as DEP/ARR. Entering them deletes any previous route and calls up the route selection page. If one airport is missing from the database, the NEW RWY page would show, but it does not work in the A32NX.
INIT REQUEST (2R): in the A32NX it loads the flight plan from SimBrief. It shows only if no flight plan is entered, so do not set a destination in the MSFS world map.

FLIGHT NUMBER (3L), COST INDEX (5L), CRZ FL/TEMP (6L): type and press the LSK. Without a cruise level the system gives no predictions on the ground. Without a temperature at the cruise level it computes ISA.
CO RTE (1L) and the company route do not work in the A32NX. ALTN/CO RTE (2L) is dashed until a destination is entered; you can enter an alternate by hand.
IRS INIT (3R) opens the page to align the IRS to the airport coordinates. WIND/TEMP (5R) opens the wind pages; TROPO (6R) is the tropopause altitude (default 36 090 ft, up to 60 000 ft).

INIT B is for the gross weight and centre of gravity before the engine start. It becomes the FUEL PRED page after the first engine starts. Open FUEL PRED with the FUEL PRED key, or with the right arrow on INIT A.

ZFW/ZFWCG (1R, INIT B; 3R, FUEL PRED): must be entered to get a speed profile and predictions. Press LSK1R once to get the computed values into the scratchpad and again to store them. 'ENTRY OUT OF RANGE' shows for a value outside the range.

BLOCK (2R): block fuel is mandatory. When entered the title changes to INIT FUEL PREDICTION. FUEL PLANNING (3R) lets the FMGC compute it (BLOCK CONFIRM* then confirms); it is not accurate yet in the A32NX.
TAXI (1L): estimated taxi fuel, default usually 200 kg. TRIP/TIME (2L), TOW/LW (4R) and EXTRA/TIME (6R) are computed and cannot be changed.

RTE RSV/% (3L): reserve fuel or its percentage of the trip fuel; ALTN/TIME (4L) and FINAL/TIME (5L) can be changed. MIN DEST FOB (6L) defaults to ALTN + FINAL; if you enter less, CHECK MIN DEST FOB shows. TRIP WIND (5R): see 'How to type data'.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/init/ (RTE RSV/%, ALTN/TIME, FINAL/TIME, MIN DEST FOB)

steps.text: FUEL PRED page: all fields are dashed before the engine start. After it you see the arrival time and EFOB at the destination and alternate, the FOB (fuel on board) and GW/CG, which you cannot change. The EFOB turns amber when below MIN DEST FOB.

mc_fpln.title: F-PLN page
mc_fpln.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/f-pln/ (Flight Plan A Page, F-PLN Page Elements)

steps.text: Press the F-PLN key. The page lists the waypoints in order with time, speed and altitude predictions. The FROM waypoint (last overflown) is at the top, the TO waypoint second, in white.
steps.why: Scroll with the vertical slew keys. Press F-PLN to go back to the beginning.

steps.text: Press the LSK on the left of a waypoint for a lateral revision. Press the LSK on the right for a vertical revision.

Between two waypoints you see the leg name, the bearing, the distance and the track. During an approach the line also gives the final descent angle: '2 - 3 degrees' means a leg of 2 NM with a flight path angle of -3 degrees.
The title shows TMPY in yellow when a temporary flight plan exists, and OFST for a lateral offset.
steps.why: Revisions made from a LAT REV page create a temporary flight plan; changes typed directly on the F-PLN page do not.

steps.text: Constraints show in magenta. After predictions an asterisk shows: magenta = the constraint will be met; amber = it will be missed (and SPD ERROR AT WPT shows). Pseudo waypoints in brackets mark vertical events: SPD LIM, T/C, T/D, S/C, S/D, DECEL.
In NAV mode the TO waypoint can only be cleared with the DIR key.
The last line gives the distance (DIST) and EFOB at the destination; EFOB is amber when below MIN DEST FOB. F-PLN B is not available in the A32NX.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/f-pln/ (F-PLN Page Elements, Flight Plan B Page)

mc_latrev.title: Lateral revision (LAT REV) page
mc_latrev.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/f-pln/ (Lateral Revision Pages, LAT REV Page Elements)

steps.text: Press the LSK on the left of a waypoint (or the airport) on the F-PLN page to open the LAT REV page of that waypoint.
steps.why: There are four types: from the origin, from the destination, from a waypoint, from the present position. SID changes are only done at the origin, STAR changes only at the destination.

steps.text: DEPARTURE (1L, origin only): select the runway and the SID. ARRIVAL (1R, destination only): select the runway, approach, STAR, VIA and transition.
HOLD (3L): set a hold at the waypoint or present position. NEXT WPT (3R): type the waypoint that follows. AIRWAYS (5R): string up to five airways after the revised waypoint.
NEW DEST (4R): change the destination (creates a temporary plan direct to it, clears the waypoints between and leaves a discontinuity). ENABLE ALTN (4L): enable the alternate flight plan.
FIX INFO (1R, only at the FROM waypoint): radial, radius and abeam intercept points. See the FIX INFO guide.
OFFSET (2L), LL XING/INCR/NO (2R) and ALTN (5L, list of alternates) are not available in the A32NX.
When the page shows TMPY, press INSERT* (LSK6R) to put the temporary plan into the active flight plan.

mc_vertrev.title: Vertical revision (VERT REV) page
mc_vertrev.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/f-pln/ (Vertical Revision Pages, VERT REV Page Elements)

steps.text: Press the LSK on the right of a waypoint on the F-PLN page to open the VERT REV page.
steps.why: Any change here makes the FMS recompute the vertical profile and invalidates the predictions. A revision that does not meet the criteria gives NOT ALLOWED.

steps.text: CLB/DES SPD LIM (2L): the speed limit for climb or descent; it is a system default, a database default or your entry.
SPD CSTR (3L): a speed constraint at this waypoint. ALT CSTR (3R): an altitude constraint; + in front is at or above, - in front is at or below.
steps.why: In take-off and climb only 'at' and 'at or above' constraints restrict; in descent and approach only 'at' and 'at or below'. Constraints apply to the climb, descent and approach, never to the cruise.

steps.text: QNH (4L, destination only): the destination QNH; it also shows on the PERF APPR page. WIND (5L): opens the wind page. STEP ALTS (5R): appears once a cruise altitude is entered (not in descent, approach or go-around).
GS INTCPT (3R, destination only) shows the glide slope intercept altitude for an ILS; you cannot change it. ALT ERROR (4R) shows by how much a constraint will be missed (more than 250 ft).
RTA (2R), the constant Mach segment fields (4L, 4R) are not available in the A32NX.
Press the PERF key: it opens the page of the current flight phase. In PREFLIGHT and DONE it opens TAKE OFF. Pages of finished phases are no longer available.
