steps.why: The phases are PREFLIGHT, TAKEOFF, CLIMB, CRUISE, DESCENT, APPROACH, GO-AROUND, DONE. PREV PHASE (6L) and NEXT PHASE (6R) show the neighbouring pages.

steps.text: TAKE OFF: V1 (1L), VR (2L), V2 (3L) stay amber until entered. Without V2 there is no SRS mode. TRANS ALT (4L) defaults from the database. THR RED / ACC (5L): thrust reduction and acceleration altitude, default 1500 ft above the runway, minimum 400 ft.

TAKE OFF, right column: FLAPS/THS (3R) the flap setting and the trim; FLX TO TEMP (4R) the flex temperature (only in preflight); ENG OUT ACC (5R) is a reminder. TO SHIFT (2R) and UPLINK TO DATA (6L) do not work in the A32NX.
If you change the runway or the take-off shift after entering V1, VR, V2 on the same airport, CHECK TAKEOFF DATA shows but the values stay.

CLIMB, CRUISE, DESCENT: they show the cost index and the managed speed. A selected speed shows after you pull the FCU speed knob; pushing the knob returns to the managed speed. Most prediction fields are not available in the A32NX. DES CAB RATE and STEP ALTS do not work.

APPROACH: QNH (1L) and TEMP (2L) are mandatory within 180 NM (amber boxes). MAG WIND (3L), TRANS ALT (4L), VAPP (5L, computed, you can change it; CLR returns the computed value), BARO (2R), RADIO (3R) and LDG CONF CONF3 (4R) for a flaps 3 landing.
ACTIVATE APPR PHASE (6L): push, and push again to confirm, to activate the approach phase. If you did it by mistake, enter the cruise flight level on the PROG page to go back to cruise.
GO-AROUND: THR RED ACC (5L) is the thrust reduction and acceleration altitude for the go-around (default 1500 ft above the destination runway, minimum 400 ft).
Press the PROG key. The title changes with the flight phase.
CRZ (1L): the cruise flight level. You can change it here. It cannot be lower than the altitude on the FCU, and it follows a higher FCU altitude. In descent and approach it shows dashes.
OPT (1M) shows the computed optimum flight level in green. REC MAX (1R) shows the recommended maximum altitude in magenta (limited to FL398).
BRG/DIST (4L and 4R): type a navigation point on the right (4R) to see its bearing and distance. It accepts an airport, waypoint, navaid or runway ident, a lat/long, a PBD or a PBX.
GPS PRIMARY (5R) shows when the FMS is in GPS PRIMARY mode. At the bottom: REQUIRED accuracy (6L, you can change it), ACCUR HIGH/LOW (6M) and ESTIMATED accuracy (6R).
Position update (3L) is not available. REPORT (2L) and Predictive GPS (5L) are not fully implemented.
Press the RAD NAV key. The page is for the radio navaids tuned for display: VOR, VOR/DME, TAC, VORTAC, ILS and ADF.

VOR1 / FREQ (1L) and FREQ / VOR2 (1R): the ident and frequency of VOR 1 and 2, auto-tuned or manual. To tune one by hand type the ident or the frequency. CLR returns to the auto-tuned navaid. CRS (2L, 2R): the courses.

ILS / FREQ (3L): the ILS ident and frequency. It is auto-tuned for the departure runway, and for an ILS approach in the flight plan when you are in climb phase or higher and within 250 NM of the destination. If your entry differs from the auto-tuned one, RWY-ILS MISMATCH shows. CRS (4L) comes automatically.

ADF1 / FREQ (5L) and FREQ / ADF2 (5R): type the ident or the frequency. The BFO function (6L, 6R) is not available. Auto-tune only works for navaids in the database. Manually tuned frequencies show in large font.
Press the DIR key. Type a waypoint into 1L, or press an LSK from 3L to 6L next to a waypoint of the flight plan.
An amber ERASE (6L) and DIRECT (6R) appear. ERASE clears the waypoint in 1L. DIRECT puts the direct leg into the flight plan as the active leg, and the aircraft starts turning at once.
steps.why: In NAV mode the active leg changes. In HDG mode, DIRECT switches to NAV for a direct course to the waypoint. The Direct guide says LSK 1L for the confirmation; use the prompt your MCDU shows.

steps.text: DIRECT TO (2R) is the default mode. ABEAM PTS (3R) and RADIAL IN/OUT (4R, 5R) are not yet implemented.
Press the SEC F-PLN key to open the secondary flight plan index. The secondary plan is used to prepare a diversion, a runway change or the next flight.
COPY ACTIVE copies the active flight plan. You can change the copy; it creates no temporary plan. ACTIVATE SEC makes it the active plan, SWAP ACTIVE swaps the two.
steps.warn: The briefing page says the SEC F-PLN is not implemented yet; the feature guide says it is available on the Development version, without predictions.

steps.text: Press the DATA key. The A/C STATUS page shows at power-up: aircraft type, engine type, active database (validity period) and, in small font, the second database. Changing the database, the IDLE/PERF factor and STATUS/XLOAD do not work in the A32NX.

DATA INDEX page 1 (navigation systems): POSITION MONITOR (FMS 1, FMS 2, radio/GPS, MIX IRS, IRS 1 to 3 with their mode INVAL, ALIGN, NAV or ATT; FREEZE/UNFREEZE in 6L), IRS MONITOR, GPS MONITOR, CLOSEST AIRPORTS.

CLOSEST AIRPORTS: the four closest airports with bearing, distance and time. You can add a fifth airport at 5L. Page 2 lets you enter a headwind (-, H or HD) or tailwind (+, T or TL) per airport for the EFOB; it is not fully available.
Page 2 (use the horizontal slew key): WAYPOINTS (1L), NAVAIDS (2L), RUNWAYS (3L), ROUTES (4L) and the stored data (1R to 4R). Up to 99 stored waypoints exist; they are not kept after the flight.

To delete a stored waypoint: open its page and use CLR on the ident. Delete all: DELETE ALL on a stored waypoint page, or on the A/C STATUS page. A waypoint in use stays and F-PLN ELEMENT RETAINED shows.
Press the MCDU MENU key. The page lists the systems: FMGC (1L, opens DATA A/C STATUS), ATSU (2L). AIDS, CFDS and NAV B/UP do not work in the A32NX.
Select ATSU, then AOC MENU: INIT/PRES (1L), WX REQUEST (2L), ATIS (3L), FREE TEXT (1R), RECEIVED MESSAGES (3R), SENT MESSAGES (4R). DIVERSION and MISC do not work.
INIT/PRES: press INIT DATA REQ* to import the SimBrief flight plan; the pages then let you review the data.

WX REQUEST: choose METAR or TAF (1L), type up to four airport codes (1R to 4R) and press SEND. ATIS: type the airport (1L), choose ARRIVAL (2L), DEPARTURE (3L) or ENROUTE (2R), then SEND. Read the answers under RECEIVED MESSAGES: press the LSK next to the message to read it.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/mcdu-menu/ (WX REQUEST Page, ATIS Page, AOC MENU Page)
steps.why: The data comes from the source configured in the flyPad settings (ATSU/AOC).

steps.text: ATC COMM (CPDLC): the FlyByWire briefing does not describe this page; it refers to the Hoppie ACARS guide.

Type I messages are a direct result of your action. Type II messages report a situation or ask for an action, and wait in a queue of up to 5. Amber is important, white is less important. Clear them with the CLR key.

FORMAT ERROR: the entry does not have the format of the field. ENTRY OUT OF RANGE: the value is outside the range of the field. NOT ALLOWED: the entry or action is not allowed in that field. NOT ALLOWED IN NAV: you tried to change the TO waypoint while in NAV.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/messages/ (FORMAT ERROR, ENTRY OUT OF RANGE, NOT ALLOWED)

steps.text: NOT IN DATA BASE: you tried to enter or call up a route, a FROM/TO pair or a place that is not in the database. AWY/WPT MISMATCH: the airway you entered does not contain the revised point; a second airway must contain the end point of the first.

CHECK TAKEOFF DATA: you changed a take-off parameter and V1, VR, V2, FLEX or the runway may no longer agree. INITIALIZE WEIGHT/CG: ZFW or block fuel is undefined after the engine start. CHECK WEIGHT: the gross weights differ by more than 7 t.
steps.source: https://docs.flybywiresim.com/pilots-corner/a32nx/a32nx-briefing/mcdu/messages/ (CHECK TAKEOFF DATA, INITIALIZE WEIGHT/CG, CHECK WEIGHT)

steps.text: ENTER DEST DATA: no wind, QNH or temperature for the destination and you are 180 NM out. CHECK MIN DEST FOB: your MIN DEST FOB is lower than ALTN + FINAL. F-PLN ELEMENT RETAINED: you tried to delete a stored item that is in use.
The full list of messages is on the FlyByWire page 'MCDU Messages'.

mc_done.title: Done
mc_done.text: Choose another page from the MCDU reference when you need it.
